author: frankbria
body:
Closes #10.

## What
Adds a prominent **True Hypnosis ↔ Plain Meditation** toggle that is persisted, pre-filled next launch, and feeds the generation spec.

- **Prominent toggle** (`HypnosisToggle`) — a two-option segmented control above the categories, each mode with a one-sentence explainer (True Hypnosis: "Direct suggestions guide you into a deep, focused trance."; Plain Meditation: "Gentle, open awareness with no hypnotic suggestion.").
- **Persisted preference** — first persistence layer in the app: `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` (Expo-Go bundled). The choice is saved on change and pre-filled on the next launch. `loadHypnosis()` returns `boolean | null` so the default (`true`) lives once in the toggle's `useState` and cleared-storage paths dispatch no redundant render.
- **Feeds generation** — `TrackSpec.hypnosis` already exists in `@lull/shared` and the API consumes it; the Sprint-0 generation path now sends `{ ...DEFAULT_SPEC, hypnosis }` so the toggle actually drives the `/script` request.
- **Hydration race guard** — a `userSetRef` (set synchronously in the setter) prevents a slow `loadHypnosis()` from clobbering a choice the user made before it resolved (codex review finding, resolved).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Prominent toggle with a one-sentence explainer each
- [x] Feeds the generation prompt; saved as a preference and pre-filled next time

## Tests
`apps/mobile`: 19 tests pass (typecheck + eslint clean, no `act()` warnings). New coverage: both modes + explainers render; default is True Hypnosis; toggling switches; persistence round-trip (save → fresh launch → pre-filled); the no-clobber guard; plus the AsyncStorage round-trip via the official in-memory jest mock.

## Known limitations
- "Feeds generation" is wired into the existing **`__DEV__`-only** Sprint-0 harness; full assembled-spec generation (components + hypnosis) is owned by **#13** (Confirm & Generate). The transient-default-before-hydration concern is unreachable on that path (a manual button tap can't beat a ~1ms storage read), so no button-gating was added — hydration gating belongs with #13's real generation UI.

author: pranixquick
body:
## F7 — security headers + Report-Only CSP

Adds an `async headers()` block to `next.config.js` (inside `nextConfig`, so it still flows through `withPWA` + `withSentryConfig`) applying to all routes:

**Enforcing (non-breaking):**
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` (clickjacking — nothing frames the app; Razorpay/Google open as child popups/iframes, unaffected)
- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
- `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=()` — camera stays available for scanning; mic/geo disabled

**Report-Only (intentionally not enforcing yet):**
- `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` with allowances for Supabase (REST + `wss`), Razorpay checkout, OneSignal, Google Fonts/OAuth, GA, Sentry, and the service worker (`worker-src blob:`).

### Why Report-Only
An enforcing CSP that misses one origin white-screens the whole app — too risky on a payment app pre-launch, especially with the domain still unsettled (F15). Report-Only logs violations to the console so we can confirm the policy is complete, then flip the header key to enforce.

### Verify after merge
Open devtools → Network → any document response → confirm the four enforcing headers are present. Watch the console for CSP violation reports; if any legitimate flow (login, Razorpay checkout, push, fonts) reports a block, we widen that directive before enforcing.

author: garthvh
body:
## Problem

Closes #1976. On iOS 18+, sending a message crashes with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` in `UIKitTextEditorCoordinator.update` → `String.UTF16View._offsetRange(for:from:)`.

The iOS 18+ compose area (`FormattingComposeArea`) binds `TextEditor`'s selection to a `TextSelection?` holding a UTF-16 range into the *current* string. Sending a message clears the field (`typingMessage = ""`), and the byte-limit guard truncates it — both programmatic mutations that leave the selection pointing into the old, longer string. On the next layout pass the coordinator maps that stale `NSRange` onto the shorter string and traps, so it crashes on every send.

The pre-iOS-18 path uses a plain `TextField` with no selection binding, which is why the crash is iOS-18-only and predates 2.7.14 (it landed with the formatting compose area).

## Fix

Drop the selection whenever the text changes programmatically:

- **Reactive** — in `onChange(of: typingMessage)`, set `textSelection = nil` when the field is emptied or truncated.
- **Proactive** — new `send()` / `alert()` / `requestPosition()` wrappers null the selection *before* the parent handlers mutate the text, so the coordinator never updates with an out-of-range selection.

Normal typing/deletion is untouched (UIKit drives text and selection together); only programmatic edits clear the selection. Builds clean for the iOS simulator.

Before this PR, in SimulatorGL.py, the placement of the tool object was temporarily modified and then reset to it's original value. Even though this left the tool in the correct state, it still caused a recompute of the tool and therefore all operations that use that tool. Every time the simulator was started. Now we just make a temporary copy of the tool and modify that. Since the tools are usually very simple geometry, just one PartDesign Revolution, there is no appreciable performance or memory penalty.

body:
## O que entrega

Fecha o ciclo aberto pela UI de pacientes: quando o nutricionista cria um paciente, ele é convidado por e-mail. Esta fatia constrói o que **recebe** esse convite.

**Fluxo do paciente convidado:**
1. clica no link do convite →
2. cai em **`/accept-invite`** e define uma senha →
3. é redirecionado para **`/download-app`** ("baixe o app") →
4. **não tem acesso ao painel web** (é só do nutricionista) — é mandado para `/download-app`.

## Mudanças

- **API:** novo env **`WEB_ORIGIN`** (obrigatório, exige scheme `http(s)`); o convite (`inviteUserByEmail`) agora passa `redirectTo=${WEB_ORIGIN}/accept-invite`.
- **`/accept-invite`** (client): consome a sessão do convite vinda no hash da URL (fluxo implícito do Supabase, via `onAuthStateChange` + `getSession`), define a senha (reaproveita o padrão do reset-password: `updateUser` → `signOut`) e vai para `/download-app`. Estado de "convite inválido/expirado" quando não há sessão.
- **`/download-app`**: tela "baixe o iNutri" com badges App Store / Google Play **desabilitados ("em breve")** — o app mobile ainda não foi publicado.
- **Bloqueio de paciente no web:** helper `isWebDashboardRole` + gate no layout `(app)` (redireciona `PATIENT` → `/download-app`). Rotas `/accept-invite` e `/download-app` adicionadas às públicas.

## ⚠️ Config manual necessária (Supabase + .env) para funcionar de ponta a ponta

- **`apps/api/.env`:** `WEB_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3001`
- **Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration:**
  - **Redirect URLs** (allowlist): adicionar `http://localhost:3001/accept-invite` ← **causa do bug original**: sem isso o Supabase ignora o `redirectTo` e cai na Site URL.
  - **Site URL:** `http://localhost:3001`

## Testes

API 142/142 · web 66/66 · `next build` verde (`/accept-invite` e `/download-app` no route table). Revisão de branch (opus) feita; ajustes aplicados.

## Fora de escopo

App mobile + links reais das lojas (badges "em breve"); fluxo `token_hash`/`verifyOtp` (abordagem A); reenvio de convite pela UI.

body:
## 问题

用 `Ctrl+Shift+Alt+E` 打开**文件浏览器侧栏**(File Explorer)后,滚轮上下滚动明显**卡顿、一顿一顿**,键盘上下键导航也一样。

## 根因

不是渲染慢/计算重,而是滚动时**漏掉了"请求重绘"**。渲染是事件驱动 + 脏门控(`render_gate.frameNeedsRender`),滚动只改了偏移量却没有置位 `g_force_rebuild`,于是这一帧被判定为"无需渲染",新位置要等下一次**光标闪烁**(每 600ms)才出帧 —— 实际刷新率掉到 **≈1.6 fps**,所以卡顿。

`handleMouseWheel` 里**其它每一支**(设置页/命令面板/AI 对话/Copilot 侧栏/预览 pane)滚动后都有 `g_force_rebuild = true`,唯独文件浏览器那一支漏了;`handleKey` 的文件浏览器键盘分支同样漏了。

详见 #287。

## 修改

- `src/input.zig` 滚轮分支:`file_explorer.scrollBy(delta)` 后置 `AppWindow.g_force_rebuild = true`。
- `src/input.zig` 键盘分支:`handleFileExplorerKey(ev)` 命中后置 `AppWindow.g_force_rebuild = true`。
- 两处都**不动** `g_cells_valid`:文件浏览器画在终端 cell grid 之上,底下终端没变,无需重建 cell grid(更省)。

## 测试(TDD,先红后绿)

新增两个回归测试,断言滚动 / 键盘导航会请求一帧:
- `input: file explorer mouse wheel scroll requests a repaint`
- `input: file explorer keyboard navigation requests a repaint`

加修复前两测均失败(`g_force_rebuild` 仍为 false),修复后转绿。

- `zig build test-full` ✅(2289 passed / 0 failed / 12 skipped)
- `zig build test` ✅

> GUI 实机滚动手感待人工确认。

Fixes #287

author: jpapiez
body:
## Summary

Implemented the highest-impact, lowest-effort optimization from the performance scan: replace full descending sorts used only to select a single latest/largest item with single-pass selection.

Changed paths:
- `src/api/Services/Maintenance/MaintenanceAlertEngine.cs`
- `src/api/Controllers/MaintenanceController.cs`
- `src/infra/Services/Gcode/GcodeMetadataExtractorService.cs`

This reduces CPU and allocation overhead in maintenance alert/upcoming-task calculations and G-code thumbnail extraction while preserving existing tie behavior for maintenance logs.

## 10 performance improvements identified

1. Replace `OrderByDescending(...).First()` with single-pass max/latest selection in maintenance log grouping and G-code thumbnail selection. **Implemented in this PR.**
2. Push System Logs Lucene/filter predicates closer to the repository/query layer instead of loading all logs before filtering.
3. Add repository-level enabled-printer query for FilaMan instead of `GetAllAsync()` followed by in-memory filtering.
4. Add `GetByPrinterIdsAsync` for printer statistics used by upcoming maintenance instead of loading all statistics then filtering.
5. Memoize `CompactPrinterCard` to avoid list-wide re-renders when parent state changes without card prop changes.
6. Memoize `DetailedPrinterCard` to reduce expensive sidebar/card re-render cascades.
7. Memoize expensive printer filtering/sorting in `PrintersPage`.
8. Reduce catalog name normalization allocations by replacing LINQ character concatenation with a lower-allocation whitespace-removal path.
9. Memoize or hoist model browser column definitions/date-size formatting where possible for large file lists.
10. Lazy-load analytics chart components / Three.js-heavy viewers to reduce initial frontend bundle and main-thread work.

## Validation

- `dotnet build ./farm-web.sln -c Debug`
- `dotnet test ./farm-web.sln -c Debug --no-build`
- `dotnet format ./farm-web.sln`

Note: the solution still reports existing NuGet vulnerability warnings during build/restore, unrelated to this performance change.

author: learning-sketch
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

PR vllm-project#10592 (`[Feature] WeightTransfer: Add NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine backend for Ascend NPU`) passed all gates but broke the smoke test with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ray'
```

**Root cause**

`vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_weight_transfer_engine.py` runs during *global plugin patching* — extremely early in startup, triggered even by `AsyncEngineArgs.add_cli_args(parser)` → `load_general_plugins()`. This happens long before any weight-transfer backend is selected.

The patch eagerly imported the engine classes at module top level:

```python
from vllm_ascend.distributed.weight_transfer.npu_ipc_engine import (
    NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine,
)
```

`npu_ipc_engine` transitively imports `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.ipc_engine`, which does `import ray` at module top level. `ray` is an optional dependency, so when it is not installed the entire `vllm_ascend` plugin load aborts and **every** `vllm serve` invocation crashes — even workloads that never use weight transfer.

Import chain that crashed:

```
vllm_ascend/__init__.py:_ensure_global_patch()
  → utils.py:adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)
    → patch/platform/__init__.py
      → patch_weight_transfer_engine.py
        → distributed/weight_transfer/npu_ipc_engine.py
          → vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/ipc_engine.py
            → import ray   # ModuleNotFoundError
```

**Fix**

Replace the eager top-level imports with lazy loader functions. `WeightTransferEngineFactory._registry[backend]` is a zero-arg callable that returns the engine class and is only invoked from `create_engine()` when the backend is actually requested. Deferring the import into those callables matches the factory's existing lazy-loading contract, so the `ray`-importing module is only loaded when the `ipc` backend is selected (at which point ray is genuinely needed):

```python
def _load_npu_ipc_engine() -> "type[WeightTransferEngine]":
    from vllm_ascend.distributed.weight_transfer.npu_ipc_engine import (
        NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine,
    )
    return NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine

WeightTransferEngineFactory._registry["ipc"] = _load_npu_ipc_engine
```

Only the `ipc` registration is made lazy, since the IPC engine is the one that transitively imports `ray`. The `nccl` → HCCL registration keeps its eager import, as `hccl_engine` has no optional-dependency import problem.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The `nccl`/`ipc` backend resolution behaves identically; only the timing of the underlying module import changes (deferred until the backend is actually used).

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m py_compile` and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass on the changed file.
- The fix removes the only eager import of the IPC engine on the global-patch path, so plugin loading no longer requires `ray`. The other registration site (`distributed/weight_transfer/__init__.py:register_engine`) already uses lazy string-based registration and was unaffected.

- vLLM version: v0.22.1
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/967c5c3bc38891f4465d3f4e99917ed837bb3833

body:
This PR enhances the eBPF CPU Guardian by adding monitoring for file deletions (`unlink` and `unlinkat` syscalls) and ensuring proper cgroup v2 initialization.

Key changes:
1. **eBPF Kernel Space**: Added handlers for `sys_enter_unlink` and `sys_enter_unlinkat`. Refined `sys_enter_execve` to use `bpf_get_current_comm` for more reliable command name capture.
2. **Behavioral Analysis**: The `Analyzer` now awards points for file deletions (10 base, 20 total for documents like .pdf, .txt, .doc). The logic has been refactored for better clarity and to resolve borrow checker issues.
3. **Cgroup Management**: `CgroupManager` now explicitly enables the `cpu` controller in the cgroup v2 hierarchy, which is required for applying CPU limits.
4. **Shared Types**: Consolidated `OpenEvent` into a more generic `PathEvent` to support multiple file-related syscalls.
5. **Testing**: Added unit tests to verify the new scoring logic for file deletions.

author: cajasmota
body:
A2 — the grammar-freshness alarm (#5411, epic #5359, milestone 0.1.4).

## What this builds

**`tools/grammar-freshness` (Go checker, standalone, zero `internal/` imports).**
Reads the committed `grammars.lock`, and for each of the 28 grammar-backed
languages queries its upstream `tree-sitter/tree-sitter-<lang>` repo's latest
**release/tag** via the GitHub API, falling back to the **default-branch latest
commit date** for repos with no releases. Compares the upstream commit date to
the bundled smacker snapshot (`2024-08-27`) and emits each grammar as
`STALE` / `CURRENT` / `UNKNOWN` (unreachable).
- Output modes: `-format table` (human, stdout) and `-format markdown` (the
  tracking-issue body).
- Resilient: rate-limit-aware (honours the reset header once), tolerates repos
  with no releases, captures per-grammar errors instead of aborting.
- Exits non-zero **only** on a hard error (unreadable manifest, or *every*
  upstream lookup failing). Finding stale grammars is reported, not a failure.

**`.github/workflows/grammar-freshness.yml`.** Monthly `schedule:` cron (06:00
UTC, 1st) + manual `workflow_dispatch`. **No push/PR triggers** (free-tier
minutes, per CI policy). Minimal permissions (`issues: write`, `contents:
read`). Runs the checker; when grammars are stale it **creates or updates a
single tracking issue**, found idempotently by the stable `grammar-freshness`
label (title fallback), so re-runs edit the same issue rather than spamming.

**Tests** (`tools/grammar-freshness/*_test.go`): an injected fake upstream
source (no live GitHub API) covers the stale / current / no-release-fallback /
errored classification, sort order, and the markdown output, plus a parse test
against the real `grammars.lock`.

**Docs/CHANGELOG:** new A2 section in `docs/grammar-freshness-audit.md`
(how the cron works + how to read the tracking issue) and a CHANGELOG
`### Added` bullet.

## Why per-grammar, not per-dependency

The smacker binding that bundles every grammar is **unmaintained** (at its own
upstream HEAD since 2024-08-27, per the B3 audit), so Renovate-on-dep (A1) is
blind. A2 tracks each upstream grammar repo **independently** — it is THE
freshness alarm.

## Dry run

A local dry run against the live API flags **24 of 28 grammars stale** (up to
~21 months behind). The 4 reported current — lua, proto, toml, yaml — have
upstreams that genuinely predate the 2024-08-27 snapshot. Most/all being stale
is the intended signal motivating the B1 catch-up bump and B2 decoupling.

Part of epic #5359. Do not merge yet — coordinator reviews + batches a CI run
before the 0.1.4 tag.

author: tonyfettes
body:
Aligns `PageCellState` to upstream Ghostty's `packed struct(u64)` — a flat 8-byte cell — closing a large part of the scroll/print throughput gap vs Zig. Five commits, each green and self-contained, building toward the final flip.

## Why

A boxed/struct cell with pointer fields copies expensively on the print/scroll hot path (immutable `with_*`, snapshots, row shifts). Earlier `#valtype` attempts *regressed* (+59% scroll) because a value cell still moved 20 bytes / retained pointers — the flat-cell win only materializes at **8 bytes**, where a copy becomes a memcpy and a row becomes a contiguous scalar buffer. Getting there requires removing every pointer/wide field from the cell first.

## The series

1. **`3da12e5` style → `StyleId`** — intern cell styles into a shared grow-only `StyleTable`; cell holds a 16-bit id, not a pointer.
2. **`fd14381` hyperlink → `HyperlinkId`** — same, into a `HyperlinkTable`; content-addressed so it's position-independent across scroll.
3. **`d2b2ede` grapheme → `GraphemeId`** — same, into a `GraphemeTable`; the cell is now all-scalar (zero pointers).
4. **`35d6655` evict the hyperlink id to a per-row side array (PR 4a)** — a `HyperlinkId` accumulates unboundedly over a session (`ls --hyperlink` mints one per file), so unlike the bounded style/grapheme ids it can't share the 64-bit budget. The cell keeps only a presence *bit*; the id moves to `link_ids` (per-row, parallel to `cells`, `None` for link-free rows). Key invariant: the side array is read only where the presence bit is set, so clear/blank paths are untouched and only cell-*moving* paths (blits, partial scroll, intra-row shifts, history harvest/reflow, resize) thread links. Resolution is now by position.
5. **`992a70d` flip to `struct PageCellState(UInt64)` (PR 4b)** — pack the four scalar fields into one word: `codepoint [0,21) · style_id [21,37) · grapheme_id [37,53) · flags [53,59)` (wide/protected/hyperlink-present/semantic). All accessors become bit ops; `pack` is the single mint point. A newtype-over-`UInt64` is a transparent scalar, so `FixedArray[PageCellState]` is a flat `u64` buffer — no `#valtype` needed.

## Results

**Workload micro-bench** (`moon bench -p bench/workloads --release --target native`), vs the pre-series baseline:

| workload | speedup | | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain_lines | **1.56×** | scroll_storm | **1.73×** |
| wrapped_blob | 1.51× | cjk_text | 1.46× |
| colored_log | 1.40× | osc_titles | 1.44× |
| scroll_full | 1.20× | mixed_realistic | 1.40× |

Pure-escape workloads (color/sgr/query storm) flat — they barely touch cells.

**Three-way harness vs upstream Zig** (32MB corpora, 120×80, net MB/s):

| workload | ours before | ours after | Zig | gap before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lines | 21.9 | **30.8** | 127.7 | 6.1× → **4.1×** |
| printable | 32.2 | **45.2** | 135.2 | 4.2× → **3.0×** |
| sgr | 36.8 | **42.0** | 116.8 | 3.3× → **2.8×** |
| cursor | 34.8 | 33.4 | 128.2 | 3.7× → 3.8× (cursor-move heavy, few cell writes) |

The two cell-heavy laggards each gained ~40% net throughput; `lines` (the biggest gap) closed from 6.1× to 4.1× behind Zig.

## Tests

561/561 pass on both `native` and `wasm-gc` after every commit. Public API change is minimal: the cell exposes `has_hyperlink()` + `with_hyperlink_present()` instead of a cell-stored id, and `@style.StyleId::from_uint16` is added to unpack the style id from the word.

author: afarris
body: Replaces the 3-player layout (two quarters + one half) with three equal 120° wedges, plus the two rendering changes that make that layout usable on device. ### 1. Equal-slice 3p layout (`1889f6d`) Three full-screen panels clipped by a draw-time angle mask and hit-tested by angle, so no containers are rotated. Labels, text rotation, counter badges, and separators all derive from the wedge angles in the layout spec. **Closes #64.** ### 2. Skip unchanged panel color writes (`5664dd1`) Style writes invalidated the whole panel even when the color was identical, so unchanged panels redrew every refresh — a full-screen redraw per wedge on the new 3p layout. ### 3. Stage frames in PSRAM (`b49fe49`) Bands were pushed to the panel as rendered, so full-screen updates swept visibly at render speed. Bands now assemble in a 253 KB PSRAM frame and push back-to-back at SPI speed (~15 ms), bounced through the draw buffer since SPI DMA can't read PSRAM. Falls back to per-band pushes if the allocation fails. The two rendering changes are bundled here because the equal-slice layout's full-screen wedge redraws are what made the old flush sweep and redundant panel writes visibly bad — they're what make the 3p view smooth rather than separate niceties. ### Depends on #99 Built on top of the multi-select branch for the matching `ui_mp.c` context, so this currently also contains #98/#99's commits; the diff collapses to these three once those merge. Merge #99 first. ### Testing - Simulator builds clean; `make generate-matrix` regenerated green (195 screenshots) — 3p absolute/centric/tabletop wedges render correctly. - `make firmware` compiles clean for ESP32-S3 (64% flash). - Flashed to hardware and verified on device: equal slices render correctly and full-screen updates snap without the flush sweep. ### Screenshots

author: xonistreal
body: ## Summary This reviews the existing editor and addresses the request to (1) make sure tools are actually implemented, (2) add **customization to all tools**, and (3) add **more Photoshop/Photopea-style features**. Previously, several tools applied hard-coded values (Threshold always `128`, Posterize always `6` levels, Smart Sharpen always `28`, date stamp/border had fixed style). Now every value-based tool opens a customizable options panel with **live preview** and **Apply / Cancel / Reset**, mirroring Photoshop/Photopea filter dialogs. ## What changed ### New customizable tool dialog framework (`main.js`) - Generic `TOOL_DIALOGS` config + dialog engine: renders sliders, color pickers, selects, checkboxes and text inputs into the Tools panel. - Debounced **live preview** rendered straight to the canvas (non-destructive until you press Apply); Cancel restores the original, Reset returns to defaults. - Handles size-changing operations (resize, border, rotate) by resizing the canvas during preview/commit. ### Tools made fully customizable - **Threshold** (level), **Posterize** (levels), **Smart Sharpen** (amount + clarity), **Date Stamp** (format, color, position, size), **Border** (white / black / custom color / film / polaroid / rounded, size). ### New Photoshop/Photopea-style tools - **Adjust:** Brightness/Contrast, Exposure (+ highlights/shadows), Levels (black/white/gamma), Hue/Saturation, Vibrance. - **Filter:** Gaussian Blur, Sharpen, Add Noise (mono/color), Pixelate, Vignette. - **Stylize:** Black & White (channel mixer), Invert (opacity), Emboss, Find Edges (Sobel), Solarize, Halftone (mono/color). - **Artistic:** Gradient Map (shadow/mid/highlight + intensity), Sepia, Color Overlay (normal/multiply/screen/overlay). - **Transform/Overlays:** Resize (scale), Add Text (content, size, font, color, position, bold, opacity). ### Engine + UI - Added pure pixel-effect functions to `effects.js`: `applyGradientMap`, `applyEmboss`, `applyEdgeDetect`, `applySepiaTone`, `applyHueSaturation`, `applyBlackAndWhite`, `applyAddNoise`, `applyColorOverlay`. - Reorganized the Tools panel into grouped sections (Transform, Adjust, Filter, Stylize, Artistic, Overlays, Library) with new CSS for dialog controls. - Removed dead helper functions (`applyImageOperation`, `invertImageData`, `thresholdImageData`, `posterizeImageData`, `addBorder`) that the dialog framework supersedes. ## Testing - `npm run build` succeeds. - Unit-smoke-tested all new pixel-effect functions in Node (output shape + finite, in-range values) — 9/9 pass. - Headless Chrome boot test confirms the app initializes and renders all 38 tool buttons across the 7 grouped sections without runtime errors.

- Provide an admin-facing UI so ADMIN users can create and manage classes (name, subject, notes, assigned teacher, active/inactive) before enrolment and import workflows are implemented.

author: mcorbett51090
body:
## What & why

Sixth run of the recurring **Claude-subreddit scan** (search Claude communities for valuable insights → propose repo additions). Research, panel decision, and build plan are recorded in [`docs/research/2026-06-23-claude-subreddit-scan/README.md`](../blob/claude/inspiring-hamilton-kidot6/docs/research/2026-06-23-claude-subreddit-scan/README.md).

## Route reality (honest)

Reddit was not directly reachable this session. The sanctioned `scripts/reddit-scan.py` (official OAuth2 API) `_die`s because `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID`/`SECRET` are unset, and every direct route hit the environment's **network egress allowlist** (`curl` → `403 Host not in allowlist: www.reddit.com`; `WebSearch allowed_domains:[reddit.com]` → 400; privacy mirrors → same 403). Per the documented workflow, the scan fell back to **unrestricted web search** of Reddit-discussion aggregations + practitioner write-ups, cross-checked against primary Anthropic docs **and this repo's own files**. Full route table in the scan doc.

> 💡 **To fix the source for future runs:** set `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID`/`REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET` in the environment, or add `reddit.com` to the network egress allowlist.

## Panel: 1 approved, 3 denied-as-covered

| # | Finding | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | OS-level Bash sandboxing (`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, deny/allow levers) | ❌ Deny — covered across 6 files (`autonomous-guardrails-research`, `containment-posture`, `claude-code-permissions`, …) |
| **H2** | **Skill authoring = progressive disclosure** | ✅ **Approve** — genuine gap |
| H3 | Subagent summary-only handoff / isolated context | ❌ Deny — `focused-task-delegation` + SOP |
| H4 | Marketplace semver / day-one audit hook | ❌ Deny — `AGENTS.md` + drift gate already enforce |

The grounding sweep **falsified** my initial instinct to approve H1 — the sandbox autonomy-unlock angle I expected to be net-new is already documented. Logged in the doc as the lesson.

## The approved addition (H2)

`docs/best-practices/` shipped authoring guides for **hooks, slash-commands, and scenarios — but none for skills**, despite the marketplace shipping **662 skills**. This adds the missing symmetric sibling, [`docs/best-practices/skill-authoring.md`](../blob/claude/inspiring-hamilton-kidot6/docs/best-practices/skill-authoring.md):

- `description` is the always-resident **discovery surface** — write the trigger, not the implementation.
- Lean `SKILL.md` body (~≤500 lines, verify-at-use); split depth into referenced sibling files/scripts (**progressive disclosure**) — grounded in the repo's own `visual-feedback-loop` (`SKILL.md` + `driver.py`), `brand-extraction`, `decision-review`.
- `allowed-tools` least-privilege.

## Scope / safety

- **Docs-only** (`docs/best-practices/*.md` + the research doc) — **no plugin version bump, no `marketplace.json` mirror, no layout change** (all paths under the already-allow-listed `docs/**`).
- Markdown-only diff (prettier excludes markdown).
- **Migration:** none — nothing in a consumer's installed plugin changes on `/plugin marketplace update`.

## Files

- `docs/best-practices/skill-authoring.md` (new)
- `docs/best-practices/README.md` (index row)
- `docs/research/2026-06-23-claude-subreddit-scan/README.md` (new — research + panel + build plan)

| method | recall@10 | QPS | bytes/vec |

author: zenetusken
body:
## What — the distill arc's stage 2 (the MVP)

The dream's **second vertical**: where it consolidates FACTS into memory, **distill** detects repeated **workflow** patterns and **proposes a durable artifact** (a command / skill) — report-then-apply. Inspired by MiMo-Code's `/distill`, but **integrated as a PHASE of the regular dream** (one skill package, frictionless — per the user), not a separate skill/command/download.

**Measure-first** validated the premise on cm's *own* transcripts (the advisor's falsifiable test): the gated release cycle recurs ≥12× (`smoke.py` 56×, `git checkout -b` 32×, `release.sh` 23×, `gh pr create` 14×, `mypy` 14×).

## How

- **`distill_scan.py`** (new stdlib) — a LIVE within-project recurrence scan (**no persisted cross-dream tally → the D1 recurrence family stays deferred**). Reuses `extract_signals`'s `_norm`/`_looks_secret`/`_window_transcripts` + `memory_status.slug_for`. Extracts assistant `tool_use` Bash commands over a ~30-day window (broader than `marker..HEAD`); **firewall FIRST**; normalizes to a CLASS **template over MULTI-LINE input** (split on `\n`/`&&`/`;`, drop pure-`cd` + leading `VAR=`, heredoc→head, quotes stripped *before* split, drop paths/branch/value args); counts recurrence (`count≥2`, ranked, capped). `--json` = DATA only (the model does the recognition). `cm distill` added.
- **The distill PHASE** (SKILL Phase 5 step 6; render → step 7): the model RECOGNIZES a coherent repeated workflow (not a single generic verb), GATES it (≥2× + stable + repeatable + clear stopping + **not-already-covered**), and **PROPOSES the SMALLEST artifact** report-then-apply. **"Create nothing" is the common, expected outcome.**

## Safety (the highest-blast-radius feature — gate-reviewed SOUND)

The script **cannot author** (DATA only). The phase **NEVER auto-writes** an executable artifact — it presents the proposal **PLAIN/un-styled**, the human confirms, and a single confirmation authorizes **ONE named artifact** (not a suite). Proposed artifacts are **genericized** (no abs paths / machine names / personal values — the firewall catches credential-*shaped* values, not machine-specific). Known gap (acknowledged): an authored artifact is outside the Phase-5 `--audit` trail → named explicitly in the closing debrief.

## Contract / gates

**Backward-compatible PATCH:** additive script + phase; **no `CycleRecord` schema/TypedDict/smoke-pin change** (the proposal is in-conversation, like Phase 4); no removed/renamed key/script/flag.

- **Spec-review** (gate-1): report-then-apply + blast-radius **SOUND**; **1 blocker** (the `cd &&` strip was wrong for the 92%-multi-line channel) **fixed + re-measured on real data**, + 5 gaps folded in.
- **Code-review** (gate-2): **no blockers, safety sound**; 2 minors fixed (firewall-assert **test-teeth**; **quote-before-split** under-merge), 1 commented (echo-led `&&` → the model ignores generic verbs).
- `python3 tests/smoke.py` → **406 passed, 0 failed** (+12: the `_template` recall guard on REAL command forms + end-to-end scan recurrence/firewall/create-nothing/contract) · `mypy` clean · `sim ✓` · `claude plugin validate --strict` ✓.

Design doc: `docs/distill-phase.spec.md` · plan: the `distill-feature-plan` memory.

author: nickysemenza
body: ## What Replaces the heavy AWS S3 SDK (`@aws-sdk/client-s3` + `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`) with [`aws4fetch`](https://github.com/mhart/aws4fetch) — Cloudflare's recommended ~6KB SigV4 `fetch` signer — for all three server-side R2 ops in `apps/web/src/server/utils/s3.ts`: - **Presigned PUT URL** — browser direct-uploads (`generatePresignedUploadUrl`) - **Server-side PUT** — external image import (`uploadToS3` via `fetchAndStoreImage`) - **DELETE** — culling pending images (`deleteS3Object`) ## Why The SDK was hundreds of KB and didn't run cleanly on CF Workers — `vite.config.ts` carried a dedicated `cfAwsSdkBrowserRedirect` plugin purely to stop it crashing in the CF SSR env (`loadConfig is not a function`). `aws4fetch` is Workers-native and runs identically in Node (vite dev) and Workers, so there's no dev/prod split and the fragile vite workaround is gone. The native R2 Workers binding **cannot** generate presigned URLs (SigV4 signing is an S3-API op, not part of the binding), so a signer is required regardless — hence aws4fetch-only rather than the binding. ## Changes (all under `apps/web/`) - **`package.json`** — drop the two `@aws-sdk/*` deps, add `aws4fetch ^1.0.20` - **`vite.config.ts`** — delete the `cfAwsSdkBrowserRedirect` plugin (function + its entry in the conditional SSR plugin array) - **`s3.ts`** — one module-level `AwsClient` (`service: "s3"`, `region: "auto"` set explicitly to avoid R2 signature/region mismatches) + an `objectUrl()` helper for the S3-API URL. **Every exported name/signature is unchanged**, so callers (`repo/image.ts`, `routers/image.ts`, `fetchAndStoreImage`) are untouched. ## Parity notes - **Presigned path signs the URL only** (`signQuery: true`) — the browser PUT supplies `Content-Type: file.type` exactly as before. `Cache-Control` on this path was already a no-op (the browser PUT never echoed the SDK's baked `CacheControl`). - **Server-import path** applies both `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control` (it sends the request itself), preserved. - Body wrapped in `new Uint8Array(...)` because `Buffer` isn't a valid `BodyInit`. ## Verification - ✅ `pnpm install`, `format:write`, `typecheck` (tsgo, both projects) - ✅ `npx knip` — clean (no unused/unlisted-dep complaints) - ✅ `pnpm run build:cf` succeeds; bundle has **zero `@aws-sdk` references**, `aws4fetch` bundled into the server chunk; `@aws-sdk` removed from `node_modules` **Not yet exercised:** live end-to-end against the real R2 bucket (presigned upload, image import, delete). Worth running before/after merge. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

body:
## Story 06.01 — Redis sliding-window burst override

Fills the burst-override hook stubbed in **04.05** with a real runtime detector — the **velocity half** of the warm-then-attack defence (time decay, Epic 03, is the other half). A sudden blast escalates the decision **regardless of posterior**, so a warmed-up sender launching an attack is caught by velocity even when each message looks borderline (PRD §Subsystem 1 step 4, §Subsystem 4).

### What lands
- **`SlidingWindowCounter`** — atomic age-out / record / count in one Lua script over a ZSET scored by event time. A *true* sliding window (entries age out one window after they happen), `PEXPIRE`-bounded so idle keys self-evict. Reusable by 06.02 keyed per content signature.
- **`RedisBurstOverride`** — per-sender windowed velocity vs the active policy's `burst_threshold`; escalates to the configured tier with `BURST_OVERRIDE`. **Degrades open** on a Redis outage (failing closed would mass-escalate legitimate mail — a self-inflicted DoS), in deliberate contrast to the cost-safe LLM budget which fails closed.
- **`BurstProperties`** (`antispam.burst`) — the window + escalate-to *mechanism*. The **threshold** lives on the `policies` row (migration **V19**, backfills `bootstrap-v1`, `CHECK >= 1`) so it is versioned and comparable per regime (shadow/replay, retrain promotion).
- **`BurstMeter`** — `antispam.burst.detected` counter tagged `escalated-to`.
- `BurstOverride.evaluate` now takes the active `Policy`, sourcing the threshold from the already-loaded regime (no second DB lookup).
- **Off by default** (`NoBurstOverride` wired) so local/dev and the Postgres-only tests never dial Redis; the hosted deploy sets `ANTISPAM_BURST_ENABLED=true` with `APP_REDIS_URL`.

### Acceptance criteria → tests
| AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| Normal-rate traffic → no override (FP guard) | `BurstOverrideIntegrationTest.steady_traffic_below_the_threshold_never_escalates` |
| Blast exceeding threshold → escalate regardless of posterior, burst reason | IT `a_blast_exceeding_the_threshold_escalates…` + `PolicyDecisionServiceTest.burst_override_escalates_beyond_the_posterior_tier…` |
| Counts age out past the window (true sliding) | IT `counts_age_out_once_the_window_passes…` |
| Threshold sourced from active policy, tunable | `RedisBurstOverrideTest.sources_the_threshold_from_the_active_policy…`, V19 |
| Recorded + observable as metric | `BurstMeter`, reason recorded by `PolicyDecisionService` |

### Verification
- Unit tests green locally (props validation, detector logic + degrade-open, counter Java↔Lua boundary).
- Testcontainers Redis IT skips locally (no Docker daemon for Testcontainers on this host) and runs in **CI**.
- Lua sliding-window semantics validated directly against real Redis via the docker CLI: blast counts up, distinct senders isolated, counts age out after the window, TTL bounded, same-member re-add idempotent.

author: iretonsean
body:
## Summary

Adds a `graphify resolve-entities <path>` subcommand that runs the existing `dedup.deduplicate_entities()` pipeline against an already-built `graph.json`, without re-extracting from source.

## Motivation

Today, entity dedup is only called inside `build()` during the normal extraction pipeline. If a graph is produced through a custom build script (e.g. one that wires the AST + semantic extraction together manually) or imported from an external source, the dedup step is silently skipped — and there's no first-class way to apply it after the fact short of re-extracting the whole corpus.

I hit this on a ~7k-file CRM archive (49k nodes, 76% isolated). The fix turned out to be one line in a custom build script that forgot to call `deduplicate_entities()` — but the only recovery path was either an expensive full re-extract or hand-rolling the dedup call against `graph.json`. This subcommand makes that recovery a one-liner.

## What's in this PR

- New `elif cmd == "resolve-entities"` block in `__main__.py` that loads `graph.json`, calls `deduplicate_entities()`, optionally re-runs clustering, and writes back. Auto-detects whether the graph uses NetworkX `links` or raw `edges` shape.
- Flags mirror `cluster-only`:
  - `--graph <path>` — custom location
  - `--backend <name>` — optional LLM for ambiguous-pair resolution (75–92 JW zone)
  - `--dry-run` — report merges, do not write
  - `--skip-recluster` — keep current community assignments
- A `.bak` of `graph.json` is written before the rewrite
- Help banner + README + CHANGELOG entries
- 4 new tests in `tests/test_resolve_entities_cli.py` covering dry-run safety, the apply path (merge + backup), the no-op case, and missing-graph error handling

## Non-changes

- The `dedup.deduplicate_entities()` function itself is unchanged — same algorithm, same guards (cross-project still disabled, code-keyed-by-ID still skipped, same-source-file constraint preserved).
- No behavior change to existing commands.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_resolve_entities_cli.py` — 4/4 pass
- [x] `pytest tests/test_dedup.py tests/test_cluster.py` — no regressions
- [x] Manually exercised on the original use-case archive (49k → 9k nodes, all in-tree dedup logic, no LLM calls)
- [x] `graphify resolve-entities . --dry-run` exits cleanly with a before/after summary
- [x] `graphify resolve-entities .` writes `.bak`, applies, and triggers re-cluster
- [x] Missing `graph.json` produces a clear error and exits 1

## Summary

Two bodies of work from this session, in separate commits.

### Auth fixes (`c721b23`)
- **Logout no longer logs you back in.** Switched to client-side `signOut` (`next-auth/react`) so the session cookie is cleared atomically; previously a surviving JWT got bounced back to `/dashboard` by the middleware redirect.
- **Auth.js v5 env vars** — `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`/`NEXTAUTH_URL` → `AUTH_SECRET`/`AUTH_URL` in `.env.example`; URL-building routes prefer `AUTH_URL` with a fallback.
- **`middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`** (Next.js 16 convention; clears the deprecation warning, route protection unchanged).

### Three onboarding on-ramps (`3b7c77e`)
All three converge on one validated, transactional persistence path (`workspace-config` + `workspace-setup`).
- **Feature 1 — raised caps:** 4–10 stages, 3–8 checklist items, 3–8 templates, 2–8 automations across the tool schema, prompt, and the new zod validator; `max_tokens` → 16k.
- **Feature 2 — template library:** curated registry + the Switchboard blueprint (7 stages / 6 templates / 6 automations / 13 custom fields). Deterministic, no AI. Shared persistence now also seeds custom fields and resolves automation stage/template refs by name in-transaction.
- **Feature 3 — paste-a-doc:** `extract_onboarding_answers` → reuse the existing generator. Upstash-rate-limited, 12k-char cap, graceful degradation (AI on-ramps hidden when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset).
- **UI:** three-option chooser + template gallery + paste-doc form.

## Verification
- `npm run test:setup` — pure-logic checks (loader, raised caps, invariants). ✅
- `npm run itest:persist` — real DB: Switchboard blueprint persists; automations resolve stage/template by name; checklist owners + 13 custom fields land; cleanup. ✅
- `npm run itest:paste` — **live end-to-end** (real Claude + DB): a process doc extracted into the six fields and generated a **9-stage / 8-template / 8-automation** workspace — which exceeds the *old* caps, confirming Feature 1 was necessary. Validates, persists, cleans up. ✅
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean throughout.

body: ## Summary Fixes Firestore transaction error on **I'm Out** during draw: > Firestore transactions require all reads to be executed before all writes ### Root cause `foldHandDrawClient` cleared the private hand (`writePrivateHandInTransaction`) **before** `primeClientPatchReads` loaded score documents for solo-win settlement. That violates Firestore's read-then-write transaction rule when folding leaves one player and triggers solo-win settlement. ### Fix On the solo-win fold path: 1. Build settlement patch 2. `primeClientPatchReads` — read all score docs 3. `writePrivateHandInTransaction` — clear folded player's hand 4. `applySoloWinInTransaction` — write settlement Same reorder applied in `functions/gameHandlers.js` `handleFoldDraw`. Also routes `soloWin` patches through `applySoloWinInTransaction` in `runDecisionStepTransaction` (decision timeout / pass paths). ## Test plan - [ ] Draw phase: tap **I'm Out** when you are last active player (solo-win path) — no transaction error - [ ] Draw phase: tap **I'm Out** with other players still in — hand advances normally

## T9.5 — Brevedad del gobernador (directiva de salida concisa)

Cierra el arco del **gobernador de tokens** (Track 9): **medir** (T9.1) → **avisar** (T9.3) → **reducir la SALIDA**.

Hasta ahora todas las superficies por turno solo acotaban la **ENTRADA** (el contexto que Musubi inyecta). Esta toca el **otro lado del presupuesto**: pide al agente responder **conciso** para recortar los tokens de las **respuestas** del modelo. Inspirada en la skill de comunidad `caveman`, pero **nativa y atada al gobernador**.

### Qué hace
- Nueva superficie por turno **`turn_brevity`** (contabilizada en el ledger holístico), con `buildBrevityNudge`/`brevityDirective` en `turn.go`.
- Config **`memory.brevity_mode`** (opt-in, default `off`):

| Modo | Comportamiento |
|---|---|
| `off` *(default)* | no inyecta nada — **sin cambios de comportamiento** |
| `lite`/`full`/`ultra` | fija el nivel; se inyecta **una vez por sesión** (la directiva persiste en contexto) |
| `auto` | solo dispara al cruzar `session_token_budget` (mismo umbral que la alerta) → **costo cero por debajo**; requiere techo `> 0` |

- Un valor inválido **degrada a `off`** (un typo nunca enciende la directiva).
- Toda directiva **preserva exacto** el código, comandos, rutas, nombres de API, versiones y flags.
- Throttle por `session_id`+modo (`loop_brevity_injected`).

### Seguridad / no-regresión
- **Opt-in puro**: con `off` (default) no cambia nada del flujo actual.
- Tests nuevos: `TestTurnBrevityManualInjectsOncePerSession`, `TestTurnBrevityAutoFiresOnlyWhenOverBudget`, `TestTurnBrevityAutoSilentUnderOrDisabled`, `TestTurnBrevityOffSilent`, `TestBrevityDirectiveLevelsDiffer`, `TestLoadBrevityModeDefaultsOff`, `TestLoadBrevityModeNormalizes`.

## Summary

Fixes `eai tenant select` (and all other interactive list prompts) which have been broken since v3.2.7 (17 June 2026).

## Problem

Commit `a8f5621` bumped `inquirer` from `12.11.1` to `14.0.2` as part of a grouped Dependabot production dep update. In v14, the `list` prompt type was renamed to `select`. The CLI code was never updated, causing:

```
✗ Prompt type "list" is not registered. Available prompt types: checkbox, confirm, editor, expand, input, number, password, rawlist, search, select
```

## Fix

- Replaced all 6 occurrences of `type: 'list'` with `type: 'select'` across:
  - `src/lib/tenant-context.ts` — `promptForTenantSelection()`
  - `src/commands/tenant.ts` — `resolveChildTenantHomeRegion()`
  - `src/commands/init.ts` — 3 prompts (company tenant, app scope, auth provider)
  - `src/commands/types.ts` — `selectTenantKey()`

## Prevention

- **Dependabot isolation** — `.github/dependabot.yml` now separates `inquirer` into its own `npm-production-interactive` group so major version bumps get a dedicated PR instead of being buried in grouped updates.
- **Prompt type smoke test** — `tests/integration/inquirer-prompt-types.test.ts` verifies all prompt types used in the CLI are registered with the installed inquirer version. Runs in CI and will catch future breaking renames immediately.

## Testing

- All 120 tests across `tenant.test.ts`, `init.test.ts`, and `types.test.ts` pass.
- New `inquirer-prompt-types.test.ts` passes.
- Manually verified `node dist/index.js tenant select` no longer throws the prompt type error.

# 概要

Phase 2 Sub-Issue 5 (Issue #305) の fix PR。
NijiTokenKiwaTest / NijiFuzz の setUp + capped deploy 経路に setPlaceholderURI を追加、 mint 経路の PlaceholderURINotSet revert を解消。

         vm.prank(owner);

author: team-github-bot
cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact When a queued `updatePlaceStatus` mutation targets a canonical ChIJ membership that still requires legacy `manual_passport_*` migration, sync failure recovery only dropped the mutation when parent list access was `'none'` (deleted/inaccessible). Users with **read-only** collaborator access hit the same unrecoverable `permission-denied` migration failure but were left queued, **blocking the entire offline sync drain loop** on every retry. **Concrete trigger:** User is demoted from editor to viewer on a shared list while an offline passport status change is pending. On reconnect, migration fails with `permission-denied`; stale recovery keeps the mutation because access is `'read'`, not `'none'`. ## Root cause PR #220 added list-access checks in the `canMigrate` branches of `shouldDropUpdatePlaceStatus`, but only compared `access === 'none'`. Other code paths already use `shouldDropForListAccess()`, which also drops `'read'` access. ## Fix Use `shouldDropForListAccess(access)` consistently in both `canMigrate` branches (not-found and permission-denied/missing-doc paths). ## Validation - Added tests for read-only blocked migration on both `permission-denied` and `not-found` error paths - `npm test -- --run src/lib/localDb/syncMutationRecovery.test.ts` — 16/16 passing

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact PR #221 added a guard that keeps `updatePlaceStatus` mutations when a membership doc reads as missing but the user can still write the list. It treated `access === 'unknown'` the same as confirmed write access. `unknown` is returned when `getDoc(lists/{listId})` fails with `permission-denied` — including when the user was fully removed from the list. Those mutations can never succeed, but they are no longer dropped. Because `drainPendingMutations` stops at the first non-droppable failure, one stuck status mutation blocks the entire offline sync queue (lists, invitations, other place changes, etc.). **Trigger:** user marks places visited offline → owner removes them from the list → manual sync or drift recovery re-enqueues cached statuses → sync fails with permission-denied → stale check keeps the mutation → queue head blocked indefinitely. ## Root cause In `shouldDropUpdatePlaceStatus`, the new missing-membership branch used: ```ts if (access === 'write' || access === 'unknown') { return false; // keep mutation } ``` Editors with confirmed write access are covered by `write` alone. Treating `unknown` as retriable conflates "cannot verify access" with "can still write", which is incorrect for revoked users. ## Fix and validation - Only keep missing-membership status mutations when list write access is **confirmed** (`access === 'write'`). - Added regression test: drops mutation when membership is missing and list access check returns permission-denied (`unknown`). **Validation:** `npm test -- --run src/lib/localDb/syncMutationRecovery.test.ts` — 14/14 passing. ## Notes on PR #221 review Manual sync re-queue intentionally pushes local visited statuses to the cloud (by design for device-only recovery). No additional change proposed there.

author: nickderobertis
body:
## What

Turn on **React Compiler** for the PWA (`reactCompiler: true` in `apps/web/next.config.ts`, via `babel-plugin-react-compiler`), and add the render-side analogue of the plugin's cachegrind instruction counts: a **deterministic render-cost harness** that measures the win.

## Why

The existing web perf lanes can't observe what React Compiler changes:
- `decision.bench.ts` is render-free by design,
- bundle-size only sees the runtime the compiler *adds* (a cost),
- Lighthouse measures a cold load with no interaction (the compiler helps *updates*, not first paint) and is wall-clock noisy.

So the deterministic delta the compiler actually produces — wasted per-interaction recomputation — had no measurement. This adds it.

## The harness

`apps/web/src/perf/render-cost.perf.tsx` renders the **real `<App>`** over an inbox and counts how many decision-surface recomputations (`requestHeadline`, `flaggedFragments`, `scriptLines`, `toolCallLines`, `triggeredRules` — the same surface `decision.bench.ts` times) each interaction does, without the compiler vs with it.

`@vitejs/plugin-react@6` transforms JSX with **oxc, not Babel** (it ignores `babel.plugins`), so the harness wires the compiler the documented way — `@rolldown/plugin-babel` + `reactCompilerPreset`, gated on `REACT_COMPILER=1` (`apps/web/vitest.render-cost.config.ts`) — to match the production build. The harness file is named `*.perf.tsx`, so it stays out of the default `test`/coverage run.

`scripts/web-render-cost.mjs` (`just render-cost`, `web:render-cost`) runs the harness both ways and diffs them; the `Performance` workflow reports the delta in the web job.

## Results (24-card inbox)

Decision-surface recomputations per interaction (lower is better):

| interaction | baseline | compiler | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Toggle shortcuts panel (unrelated state) | 72 | 0 | −100% |
| Arrow-key inbox navigation | 72 | 0 | −100% |

Cost (supporting context): **first-load JS bundle flat**, total client JS **+3.45% gzip** (~7 kB of inlined memo caches) — not on the critical path. Profiler commit time roughly halved (wall-clock, noisy — context only).

## Verified locally

`fmt-check`, `lint` (biome + knip), `typecheck`, unit `test` (coverage holds: 98% lines / 91% branches), and the production `build` (Turbopack, with the compiler) all pass. Playwright e2e was **not** run locally (needs browsers + the Rust binaries) — CI covers it.

author: effortlesssteven
body:
Closes #2605.

## Root cause
The two positive safe-delete-warning tests poll the captured output for the `window/showMessage` notification with a **250 ms** deadline. The request handler enqueues the warning *synchronously*, but it is flushed by a separate **outbound writer thread**; under parallel test load (`RUST_TEST_THREADS > 1`) the writer is CPU-starved and the flush lags the request response, exceeding 250 ms (~66.67% flake rate in main, blocking the `unit_routed_full` / pr-fast gate).

## Fix
Generous **5 s** deadline (`wait_for_method_with_timeout`) for the two positive waits — returns immediately on first sight, fails fast on a genuinely missing notification. Test-only; the production notification path is unchanged.

## Why not drop-to-flush
The deterministic idiom elsewhere in this crate is `drop(server)` to join+flush the writer. It does **not** apply here: the `with_output` test-server constructor does not join the writer on drop (verified — drop-then-read found nothing 10/10), so a generous deadline is the correct shape for this async notification.

## Verification
Passes under representative parallelism (≤4 threads). Pathological full-core saturation on a loaded workstation can still exceed the deadline, but that is a machine-overload artifact, not the notification path. **This PR's own `unit_routed_full` gate on an isolated runner is the real arbiter.**

author: chufleco
body:
## What's Changed

### BLE
- **New `POST /api/system/ble-reset-pair` recovery endpoint.** Recovers a phone from the "Pairing rejected by SentryUSB-XXXX" dead end — the case where the phone has no Bluetooth-settings entry to forget and the only prior fix was SSH'ing in by hand.

The endpoint clears **only phone-side pairing state** so a fresh claim can succeed:
- removes each phone GATT-client bond from BlueZ (`bluetoothctl remove` + on-disk dir cleanup, so a stale LTK can't linger)
- deletes the app PIN, returning the device to the unclaimed state
- restarts **only** `sentryusb-ble.service` (the phone-facing GATT server)

### Safety
- The Tesla peer (advertised `S<hex>C`, stored keyless — the vehicle uses app-layer crypto, not an LE bond) is detected and **preserved**, along with any keyless cache entries.
- Neither `bluetooth.service` nor the telemetry sampler is restarted, so keep-awake / archiving stay running untouched.
- The companion app generates and pushes a fresh PIN during the subsequent re-claim.

## Notes
Pairs with the cold-start flag fix (separate PR) to make BLE setup recoverable end-to-end without a terminal.

On the Properties tab, the live preview sits in a sticky `overflow: auto` / `max-height` container. Fixed by:

body:
## Summary
Adds a reusable shared-opponent policy benchmark path so candidate checkpoints can be compared against the same opponents, seats, and seed range instead of relying on aggregate self-play manifest win rates with different benchmark sets.

## Task Attempted
Address the roadmap gap identified after the warning-audit comparison: cold-start and teacher-bootstrap aggregate benchmark win rates were not directly comparable because the benchmark opponent sets differed. This PR adds the command shape needed to run direct shared-opponent comparisons before choosing an incumbent candidate.

## Changes Introduced
- Added `policy_benchmark_matchups(...)` to build mirrored candidate-vs-opponent benchmark matchups from arbitrary policy specs.
- Extended `rollout_cli benchmark` with repeated `--policy`, repeated `--opponent-policy`, and `--include-policy-head-to-head` flags while preserving the existing default baseline benchmark behavior.
- Reject duplicate candidate policy ids and candidate/opponent policy-id collisions up front so shared-opponent comparisons cannot silently drop an opponent or mis-aggregate head-to-head rows.
- Exported the new helper from the package root.
- Documented the shared-opponent benchmark command and distinct `policy_id` requirement in the CPU roadmap and bootstrap strategy docs.
- Added focused tests for matchup construction, duplicate policy-id rejection, candidate/opponent collision rejection, head-to-head guard behavior, custom CLI wiring, and invalid opponent-only CLI usage.

## Risk Assessment
Low to medium. Existing default benchmark behavior is preserved when no `--policy` flags are provided. The new custom path loads policy specs before launching games and fails fast if policy ids are not distinguishable, because benchmark labels and head-to-head aggregation are keyed by policy id.

## Verification Evidence
- `./.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_collection` passed: 31 tests.
- `./.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests` passed: 679 tests, 3 skipped.
- `git diff --check` passed.

- Real local CLI smoke passed against `/Users/scott/workspace/pokerena/vendor/pokemon-showdown` with the latest cold-start and teacher-bootstrap checkpoints, `--games 1`, shared `random-legal`/`simple-legal` opponents, and candidate head-to-head enabled: 10 total games, 0 capped games. This smoke validates command wiring only, not strength.
- Claude adversarial review completed. Follow-up changes addressed the material findings by documenting/failing on policy-id collisions, enforcing candidate head-to-head requires at least two candidates, adding missing tests, and cleaning CLI help text.

author: ealanisln
body:
## ⚠️ DRAFT — gated, not for merge

Scaffolding for **Track D** (`persistent-gps-background`) — the native background-GPS app. Drafted ahead of a go/no-go so it's ready to build the moment the prerequisites land. **Do not merge** until:

- [ ] Native-app **go/no-go** decision
- [ ] **Apple Developer account** ($99/yr) + **Android keystore**
- [ ] A real **iPhone** and **Android** test device

Full evaluation: `docs/ready-set/specs/2026-06-17-native-driver-app-background-tracking.md`.

## Why a native shell

Web GPS physically can't track in the true background — iOS suspends background JS + geolocation, service workers can't geolocate. The June-22 ask ("persistent signal like Waze") needs a native location service. PR #460 hardened the **foreground** trail; this is the **background** piece.

## Approach (thin wrapper, ~0% UI rewrite)

A Capacitor shell loads the **deployed** `/driver` web UI in a WebView (`server.url`), and the community **background-geolocation** plugin keeps a location service alive in the OS background, posting each fix to the **existing** `POST /api/tracking/locations` with the driver's Supabase **Bearer** token.

**Zero backend change** — `withAuth` already accepts Bearer (`src/lib/auth-middleware.ts`) and the body matches the web client, so points land in `driver_locations` and feed shift mileage exactly like the foreground path.

## What's in here

- `native/driver-app/` — `capacitor.config.ts` (appId + `server.url` + webDir), `package.json` (Capacitor 6 + `@capacitor-community/background-geolocation`), `www/index.html` fallback, and a **README runbook** (prereqs, setup, on-device `WALK-TEST-SF` test procedure, iOS/Android permissions, productionizing → transistorsoft + TestFlight/APK).
- `native/driver-app/web-integration/capacitor-tracking.ts` — the WebView-side bridge: `addWatcher` → throttled POST, **feature-detected no-op on plain web** (safe to import unconditionally) + a wiring guide for `DriverTrackingContext`.
- `tsconfig.json` — excludes `native/` from the Next typecheck (the only change to existing files).

## Not done here (by design)

No runtime change to the Next app — the web-side bridge is drafted, not yet wired in (that's step 3 of the integration guide, done when greenlit). Native projects (`ios/`, `android/`) are generated via `npx cap add` and gitignored. `pre-push-check` green; web build unaffected.

author: alexandre-damas-murata-extra
body:
## Contexto

Após o merge do #16, o `auto-version` falhou no merge para `staging` com `npm error Version not changed` ([run](https://github.com/Mintly-Autonomos/MintlyLib/actions/runs/28074121512)), bloqueando o bump e, consequentemente, o `publish`.

## Causa raiz

No step **"Bump de versão (staging — sufixo -preview)"**:

```bash
npm version patch --no-git-tag-version   # 2.2.1-preview -> 2.2.1 (só finaliza, não incrementa)
BASE=$(... | sed 's/-.*$//')             # BASE = 2.2.1
git checkout -- package.json ...         # reverte -> 2.2.1-preview
npm version "2.2.1-preview"              # alvo == atual -> "Version not changed"
```

`npm version patch` sobre um prerelease `X-preview` só **finaliza** para `X` (não incrementa o número). Com staging já em `-preview` e bump `patch`, o alvo `${BASE}-preview` fica idêntico à versão atual → erro. Acontece em **todo PR de nível `patch`** mergeado em staging (o `ci(deploy):` do #16 foi classificado como patch). Bumps `minor`/`major` não eram afetados.

## Correção

Normaliza para a base de release antes de aplicar o bump, garantindo incremento real e versão `-preview` única a cada merge (também evita publish de versão duplicada no npm):

```bash
CURRENT=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
RELEASE=${CURRENT%-preview}
npm version "$RELEASE" --no-git-tag-version --allow-same-version
npm version <bump> --no-git-tag-version
NEXT=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
git checkout -- package.json package-lock.json
npm version "${NEXT}-preview" -m "chore(release): %s [skip ci]"
```

Simulação:

| Atual | bump | Resultado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2.2.1-preview` | patch | `2.2.2-preview` |
| `2.2.1-preview` | minor | `2.3.0-preview` |
| `2.1.0` | patch | `2.1.1-preview` |
| `2.1.0` | major | `3.0.0-preview` |

  After: only the volunteer list + Learn More button have the max-h-0 → max-h-[200px] transition. This section is hidden when collapsed and animates open when expanded, while the name/priority section above it is always fully visible.

Remove `TargetServerLayout` and `TargetDirectoryLayout`, which bundled

  provider, preserving cross-server tab behavior.

a directory-backed route (session or draft) is active.

body:
## proof_class — make the default verdict's honesty load-bearing (compose-verify trust audit)

Third and apex audit of the trust-substrate sweep. Verdict: **broken** — the most severe of the three, but the cause is the threat-model issue the gate-honesty reckoning already named.

### The critical finding (reproduced, bead `b0p`)
The top-level proof-of-run gate's default verdict (no `--legba`/`--poteau`) is **self-consistency over agent-writable files**. The panel hand-assembled a run dir and got `valid_run` exit 0 with **no key, no runtime**. Confirmed at the source: check 2 only tests file existence (content never parsed), `compute-id` re-hashes the agent's own bytes, `--poteau` is skipped when unarmed, `--legba` can never certify (no trust-store provisioning). Also confirmed: **78 agent-readable gatekeeper private keys** on disk — Form A residue (bead `p3r`).

The header is honest that its threat is the *lazy* inline-faker (against which self-consistency works). The gap: the headline `valid_run`/exit-0 was identical whether crypto ran or not.

### What this ships
Every verdict now carries `proof_class` — `"self_consistency"` (default) vs `"cryptographic"` (`--legba` rooted **or** armed `--poteau` chain verified) — plus a loud stderr warning when a `valid_run` rests only on self-consistency. Additive (no field/exit-code breakage). A consumer gating on exit 0 can now tell "not an inline fake" from "cryptographically authored."

It does **not** make the default cryptographic (that needs trust-store provisioning — `b0p`, deliberate). It stops the gate from *implying* it did.

Report: `grimoires/loa/reports/compose-verify-trust-audit-2026-06-24.md`

## Summary

- Seed the default `morning_briefing` proactive cron job disabled instead of enabled.
- Keep the existing schedule, prompt, agent id, delivery, and user opt-in path through `cron.update` unchanged.
- Add explicit seed regression coverage for disabled-by-default, idempotency, and no enabled billable agent cron jobs after fresh onboarding seed.

## Problem

- Fresh onboarding currently creates `morning_briefing` as an enabled daily proactive agent job.
- That job can run a full billable agent turn daily without explicit user opt-in.
- The existing `tinyplace_autopilot` seed path already treats autonomous spend as opt-in and creates the job disabled atomically; morning briefing should follow that same default-off posture.

## Solution

- Pass `enabled=false` when creating the seeded `morning_briefing` job via `add_agent_job_with_definition`.
- Preserve explicit opt-in through the existing Settings/Routines toggle, which already calls `cron.update` with `enabled=true`.
- Cover the seed path with a unit test that verifies the briefing is created disabled, has the expected agent id/schedule, remains idempotent, and no freshly seeded agent cron job is enabled.

author: basilechretien
body: ## Why Follow-up to the email-signature badge (#268). A user pasted the signature into **classic Outlook for Windows** and got the badge image **but it wasn't clickable** — only the text link below it worked. That's a [well-documented Outlook behaviour](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4635418/email-signature-rejects-new-links-on-images): on **paste**, Outlook keeps hyperlinks on *text* but **strips them off *images***. Our copied HTML links the image correctly (it's clickable in Gmail/Apple Mail) — Outlook's signature *paste sanitizer* drops it. ## What A **"Download for Outlook (.htm)"** option in the same Email-signature panel. Outlook reads a signature **file** directly — there's no clipboard paste, so the `` around the badge survives and the **image stays clickable** with zero manual linking. - **`outlookSignatureDocument()`** (`emailSignature.ts`) wraps the existing signature fragment in a complete, minimal HTML document suitable for a classic-Outlook signature file. Pure + tested. - **`ShareControls`**: a nested "Classic Outlook: download a file" disclosure with a **Download (.htm)** button — a client-side `Blob` download named `SigmaCV.htm` — plus concise install steps. - The badge `` gained a **`border="0"`** attribute so Outlook draws no blue link-border around the hyperlinked image. - **i18n**: 6 new keys × all ten locales (summary, why, button, 3 install steps). Install path uses `%APPDATA% ▸ Microsoft ▸ Signatures` (no backslashes). ### Scope (honest) Only **classic Outlook for Windows** reads signature files from disk, so the download targets it specifically — which is exactly the version researchers use on institutional Windows machines, and the one that strips pasted image links. **New Outlook / Outlook on the web / Mac** are cloud-based (no file import), but they generally keep the pasted image link already. A single file can't cover all of them — Microsoft doesn't expose a file-based signature on the cloud versions. ## Test plan - [x] `npm run typecheck` clean - [x] `npm run coverage` — **2131 tests pass**, gate green (stmts 98.36 / branches 91.03 / funcs 99.52 / lines 99.33) - [x] New unit tests: `outlookSignatureDocument` (full-doc structure + the verbatim `` that keeps the image clickable), `border="0"` on the badge - [ ] Manual (needs a published CV): Share ▸ Email signature ▸ Classic Outlook ▸ Download → drop `SigmaCV.htm` in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Signatures` → restart Outlook → pick the SigmaCV signature → confirm the badge is a **clickable** image > Non-English install steps are machine-drafted (consistent with the rest of `badgeUi.ts`) — flag for native review. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added "Download for Outlook (.htm)" option for email signatures compatible with classic Outlook on Windows * Email signature badge now includes proper formatting to prevent unwanted link styling in Outlook * New collapsible section with installation instructions for the Outlook file-based workflow * **Documentation** * Updated changelog with new Outlook email signature download feature details * **Tests** * Added test coverage for Outlook signature file generation and formatting

author: thejefflarson
body:
Two small CI changes from the "speed up the clippy step" thread.

## 1. Add clippy (fast — replaces the standalone build)
Swaps `cargo build --locked` for `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` in the `server` job. clippy is check-speed (no codegen) and gates the compile just like `build` did, while `cargo test` already does the real codegen — so this **adds lint coverage without adding a compile pass** (if anything slightly faster). Only the workspace crate runs through clippy-driver; deps still compile via sccache. `-D warnings` matches the repo's warnings-as-errors policy.

The codebase was already clean except one lint (`too_many_arguments` on a test histogram helper), silenced with an `#[allow]`.

## 2. Stable shared-key on rust-cache
The default rust-cache key is scoped per job + branch, so a PR's first run compiles cold. A fixed `shared-key: watcher-server` makes every run converge on one cache entry, so PRs restore main's warm `target/`.

## Validated locally
`cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean (EXIT 0); `cargo fmt --check` clean; YAML valid.

author: mshanemc
body:
## Problem

The review-diff per-finding verifier was dropping too much. Its opening instruction:

> a finding survives only if its premise is demonstrably true **AND acting on it adds value beyond what CI/automation already provides**

That `AND` clause let the verifier drop *true* findings whose value it couldn't independently prove — precisely the taste-level style/architecture findings a human reviewer makes (reuse an existing service instead of a wrapper, prefer an Effect idiom, parallelize, fewer short-term consts). The `downgrade` rule had the same leak via "no user-facing impact."

Observed on PR #7565 (apex-testing Effect refactor): review-diff ran, but findings like "use `ConnectionService.getConnection()` instead of the `getConnection` wrapper in-Effect" and "don't hand-roll duration; spans auto-time" never survived verification — they're true but the verifier couldn't prove the payoff, so they were dropped/downgraded. The human reviewer had to make every one of those comments by hand.

## Fix

Invert the burden of proof. The verifier's job is to **disprove** a finding, not to justify it.

- **drop** ⇔ affirmative disproof only: premise false (read code), already CI-covered (read workflows), or zero-consumer (gh search). "Can't see the value" / "both forms work" / "it's just style" is a **KEEP**, never a drop.
- **downgrade** ⇔ *proven* lower impact (e.g. path behind an off-by-default flag), not "seems minor."
- otherwise **confirm at the claimed severity** — the default outcome, explicitly including true-but-unprovable-value style/architecture findings.

Drop categories are unchanged (false / CI-covered / zero-consumer) — all three are evidence-based disproof. Only the value-judgment escape hatch is removed.

## Changes

Single file, `.claude/workflows/review-diff.js`:
- rewrite `verifyFindingPrompt` verdict rules
- update `VERIFY_SCHEMA` verdict comments
- update the orchestration comment above the Verify phase

`node --check` passes. No schema/control-flow change — `confirmed` with `severity == claimed` already flows through the existing fixer (which already says "'Low value' is NOT a reason to skip").

## Problem

Uploaded files return 403 Forbidden when accessed because the `thomasunderpar-media` bucket is private and the route was constructing plain public URLs (e.g. `https://bucket.t3.storageapi.dev/key`) that require public read access to resolve.

## Solution

After a successful `PutObjectCommand`, the route now creates a `GetObjectCommand` for the same key and calls `getSignedUrl` from `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` with `expiresIn: 86400` (24 hours). The resulting pre-signed URL is returned instead of the public URL, granting temporary authenticated access without changing the bucket's ACL. The `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` package was added to `package.json` at the same version range as the existing S3 client.

- **Modified** `app/api/upload/route.ts`

author: os-zhuang
body:
## Problem
The AI-built object **New** create form keeps showing the original field set after a field is added via the AI flow and published — it survives normal reloads and IndexedDB/localStorage clears.

## Root cause
`GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name` is served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, so the browser HTTP-caches the object schema for up to an hour **without revalidating**. The create form (`ModalForm`) reads the schema via `ObjectStackAdapter.getObjectSchema` (a default `fetch`) → served the stale body. The **list** endpoint `/meta/object` is uncached, which is why list views refresh on publish but the create form doesn't. The server itself is fresh (new ETag after publish — confirmed via a cache-bypass fetch), so this is the HTTP cache, **not** registry staleness.

## Fix
- **data-objectstack** — `getObjectSchema` now reads via `fetchObjectSchemaFresh()` with `cache: 'no-cache'`, forcing an `If-None-Match` revalidation (fresh schema on change, cheap `304` when unchanged). + unit test.
- **app-shell `MetadataProvider`** — the publish/install (`emitMetadataRefresh`) pulse also clears the shared adapter's metadata cache, so open forms refresh without a page reload.

## Verification
E2E in the local stack: built a Leave Request app, added + published Department then Position; the published app's create form showed all fields **with no hard reload**, while a default-cache probe still returned the stale schema (proving the fix bypasses it). Unit suites: data-objectstack 209/209, MetadataProvider 11/11.

## Follow-up (framework, separate)
The principled root fix is server-side: change that endpoint's `Cache-Control` to `no-cache`/`must-revalidate` (and fix the malformed `public, max-age, max-age=3600`) so all consumers/CDNs revalidate. This PR fixes the console symptom.

author: tareknaser
body:
### Description

`build_expr_from_value` in `entity_builder/build_expr.rs` turns token claims into Cedar expressions. It checks the JSON type in every branch except the one for extension values, which just calls `src.as_str().unwrap()`. So a token whose extension claim isn't a string panics the authorize call. This PR makes that branch reject the wrong type the way all the others do.

#### Implementation Details

- In `jans-cedarling/cedarling/src/entity_builder/build_expr.rs`, swap the `src.as_str().unwrap()` in the extension branch for the same `ok_or_else(|| TypeMismatchError { ... })?` the `String` branch right above it uses. A wrong-typed extension claim now returns a `TypeMismatchError` instead of panicking. The caller already knows what to do with that: a required attribute fails the entity build, an optional one gets skipped, same as any other wrong-typed claim.

The creative differentiator — intelligence **only we can show for free**, because HyperLiquid is on-chain so every trader's positions are public.

## What
- **Backend** `GET /terminal/perps/whales` — samples the top ~60 accounts off the HL leaderboard (cached 10m), reads their live `clearinghouseState` positions for a coin, and aggregates **long-vs-short notional** among smart money. Returns the biggest individual whale positions with the **exchange-computed liquidation price** + unrealized PnL, plus **squeeze fuel** (short notional that liquidates *above* mark → fuel for a rip) vs **downside** (long notional liquidating below).
- **SmartMoneyPanel** (4th "Smart Money" tab on the perps desk) — a positioning gauge + plain-language read ("Smart money heavily short"), squeeze-fuel tiles, and a whale table with leverage, entry, **distance-to-liquidation bars**, and uPnL.
- `usePerpsWhales` hook + types + dev-mock fixture.

## Why it's different
Coinglass-style smart-money/liquidation intel is a paid product. On HL it's **public on-chain data** — this reconstructs it natively and free.

## Verification
- `tsc` clean; `terminal.py` black-clean + parses.
- Ran the aggregation against **live HL data**: ETH whales were **100% short by notional** ($22.3M short vs $0.1M long), e.g. `0xecb6` short $14M @ 15x, `0xfc66` short $8M @ 20x on +$255K. Real, actionable signal.
- Ran the terminal — gauge, squeeze-fuel tiles, and whale table render with distance-to-liq bars.

author: runceel
body:
## What

Fixes a shipped bug in the `migrating-reactiveproperty-to-r3` skill and adds a **validated, step-by-step GitHub Copilot CLI migration guide** to `docs/docs/advanced/r3-migration.md`.

Both changes came out of an end-to-end evaluation: a sample ReactiveProperty WPF app was actually migrated to R3 + the `ReactiveProperty.R3` bridge using the real `copilot` CLI with realistic, incremental user prompts (not blanket delegation).

## Findings & changes

**1. Top finding — skill was silently dropped (FIXED).**
`SKILL.md` frontmatter had an unquoted YAML `description:` containing `: ` (in `(references/rules.json): everything ...`). YAML parses `: ` as a mapping separator, so the frontmatter failed to parse and the CLI **silently dropped the skill** from `<available_skills>`. This affected every consumer. Fix: wrap the description in a single-quoted scalar (text unchanged). Verified loading via the CLI request-payload log (count 0 → present).

**2. Install-path guidance + robustness.**
During the eval the agent intermittently mislabeled an out-of-tree read of `references/rules.json` as a "content-exclusion policy" block. Root cause: the structured file-view tool is scoped to the working tree, and the skill was installed under `~/.copilot/skills/` (outside the project). Verified (Probe E) that installing into the project's `.agents/skills/<name>/` keeps `rules.json` in-tree and reads it friction-free (and the skill auto-loads from there).
- Doc now recommends the in-tree `.agents/skills/` install first (matches `skills/README.md`), with `~/.copilot/skills/` as the cross-project alternative.
- `SKILL.md` hardened with a short note: `rules.json` ships with the skill and is not policy-excluded; if a structured read is denied for an out-of-tree install, read it another way and never report a false content/policy block.

## Evidence

- Validated the rules table actually drove the migration: a log-verified plan run cited **17 distinct ruleIds that exist only in `rules.json`** (none in `SKILL.md`).
- Sample app: baseline builds + tests green (13/13); fully migrated app (R3 + bridge) builds + tests green (13/13). Both manual-review cases (`RP-MANUAL-MODE`, `RP-MANUAL-SCHEDULER`) were correctly flagged, not guessed.
- Skill-accuracy nuance documented: R3 `EnableValidation` validates lazily, so the migration uses `ValidatableReactiveProperty` where eager validation is required (flagged + justified).

## Notes

- The `ReactiveProperty.R3` / `ReactiveProperty.R3.WPF` bridge packages are **not yet published**; the doc notes this and the lab consumed them via project references in the meantime.
- The doc itself is written for the intended NuGet experience (`dotnet add package R3 / ReactiveProperty.R3`).
- VuePress build verified.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
