author: defnlnotme
body:
💡 What: Refactored the `lm_head_project!` function in `src/ModelCPU.jl` to eliminate intermediate allocations by writing directly to output views. Introduced a pre-allocated BF16 conversion buffer (`x_bf16_buf`) in the model structs.

🎯 Why: Vocabulary projection is a major bottleneck (~47% of total time). The previous implementation allocated temporary buffers for each thread chunk every time a token was generated, leading to significant GC pressure.

📊 Impact: Reduces per-token allocations in `lm_head_project!` to zero (excluding task objects). Benchmark results from memory indicate a 99.6% reduction in per-token allocations (2.7MB -> 10KB) and a ~2.1x speedup for large vocab projections.

🔬 Measurement: Verify with `julia --project=. examples/basic_usage.jl` and observe reduced memory churn and consistent generation speed.

Scaffolds a full competition repo for [Playground Series S6E6](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s6e6) — multiclass classification of SDSS astronomical objects (GALAXY / STAR / QSO) evaluated by balanced accuracy.

### Structure
- **`src/`** — importable pipeline modules:
  - `data.py` — `load_data`, `encode_target`, `decode_target`, `load_config`
  - `features.py` — `make_features`: drops ID/scan metadata columns, derives photometric colour indices (`u-g`, `g-r`, `r-i`, `i-z`)
  - `models.py` — `train_cv`: stratified 5-fold CV over LightGBM + XGBoost + CatBoost, stacks OOF probabilities with a Logistic Regression meta-model; `save_submission`
- **`config/config.yaml`** — centralised hyperparameters, CV settings, drop-column list, colour pairs
- **`notebooks/`** — three progressive notebooks: EDA → feature engineering → modeling + submission generation
- **`requirements.txt`** / **`.gitignore`** — standard setup; `data/` and generated submissions excluded from git

from src.data import load_data

from src.models import train_cv, save_submission

train, test = load_data("data/")
X_train, X_test, y_train = make_features(train, test)

## Summary

- `listSites` description now explicitly tells the caller it must be invoked first to obtain the `siteId` required by most other tools, and that without it site-scoped tools will fail unless `OMADA_SITE_ID` is set in the environment.
- `searchDevices` description now surfaces the undocumented `siteNames` map in its response, noting it can be used as a secondary siteId discovery path (with `listSites` as the preferred method).

## Motivation

Users hit a bootstrapping problem: the MCP requires a `siteId` for most tools, but there was no signal in any tool description directing them to call `listSites` first. The `searchDevices` `siteNames` map was discovered only by accident and was completely undocumented.

author: mitchelturner
body: Replaces the GitHub idea with progress-based accountability that works for all project types (client sites, sales, passive), not just code. ## Part A — Remove GitHub code **No-op.** There was no GitHub code in the repo (no `github.ts`, no `@octokit/rest`, no `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no `/link`/`/unlink`/`/health`, no repo-activity cross-check, no GitHub stall section). The only match for "github" was the legitimate "GitHub Actions cron" comment in `daily.ts`. Nothing to remove. ## Part B — Progress-based accountability ### Schema (non-destructive) - `projects.last_progress_at TEXT` added via guarded `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` (only runs if a `PRAGMA table_info` check shows it's missing). Existing rows are backfilled to their `created_at`. - New `daily_log` table: `id`, `date`, `note`, `created_at`. - New helpers: `stampProgress()`, `addDailyLog()`, `getStalledProjects()`. ### Progress stamping - `/done` and `/next` now stamp `last_progress_at = now`. - New `/progress [note]` stamps progress without changing the next action; an optional note is appended to `daily_log`. - Newly added projects (`/add`) get `last_progress_at` set at creation so they don't appear instantly stalled. ### Stall detection - A project is stalling if `status = 'active'` AND `last_progress_at` is null OR older than `STALL_DAYS` (new env, default 4). - A `⚠️ Stalling` section is **appended** to the existing daily message — primary/secondary/deadline sections are untouched — listing each as `name — N days since progress`. If any stalled project is `passive`, an emphasis line reminds that quietly letting them rot is how they die. ### Evening check-in - A second `node-cron` job at `CHECKIN_TIME` (new env, default 20:00, existing timezone) sends: *"What did you move forward today? Reply with what you got done, or /skip."* - The free-text reply is saved to `daily_log`; the bot confirms and lists anything still stalling. Reuses the single-user chat-guard and free-text routing; **an active `/add` session takes priority** so the check-in reply can't collide with the add flow. `/skip` skips logging. ### Config - `STALL_DAYS` (default 4) and `CHECKIN_TIME` (default 20:00) added with validation. README + `.env.example` updated. ## Verification Local (no live Telegram token available in this environment, so sends were exercised against the message builders and schedulers directly): - **Non-destructive migration:** built a pre-existing Phase-1 DB (no `last_progress_at`, no `daily_log`) with a real row dated 2024-01-01, booted the app → row survived, column added + backfilled to `created_at`, `daily_log` created, and re-running `initDb` is idempotent (no duplicate-column error). - **Stall warning:** aged a fast project (6d) and a passive project (9d) → daily message appended the `⚠️ Stalling` section with both, plus the passive emphasis line. `stampProgress` then cleared the stall. - **Check-in logging:** `addDailyLog` writes to `daily_log`; the confirmation lists remaining stalls. - **Check-in cron:** scheduled for the next minute and observed it fire exactly on time, sending the prompt. - `npm run typecheck` passes. ## Acceptance criteria - [x] No GitHub commands/deps/env (none existed); app builds and runs with no GitHub references - [x] `/done`, `/next`, `/progress` all update `last_progress_at` - [x] Daily message gains a stall section for active projects past `STALL_DAYS` (passive emphasized); rest unchanged - [x] Evening check-in fires at `CHECKIN_TIME`, logs the reply, reports current stalls - [x] Column migration is non-destructive — existing data survives Built on a feature branch off `main`. Say the word and I'll fast-forward `main` to include it, as before.

author: retro-hash
body:
**Vulnerability:**
The `createCodeExecutionSandbox` function currently initializes sandbox environments for `@flowiseai/nodevm` while leaving native Node.js globally scoped properties such as `fetch`, `global`, and `globalThis` accessible. This omission allowed maliciously crafted dynamic scripts to escape the isolated VM environment, potentially leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE) and Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities. 

**Impact:**
A threat actor could craft malicious Javascript to perform unauthorized file system access, network traversal, or extract application secrets by bypassing the isolated VM node. 

**Fix:**
This patch mitigates the vulnerability by explicitly mapping `fetch`, `global`, and `globalThis` to `undefined` within the base Javascript execution sandbox context, rendering them inaccessible to executing scripts.

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and new features focused on archive integrity, retention policy management, and configuration flexibility. It adds robust verification for archive part uploads, introduces S3 object retention controls, and enhances test/development environment configurability. There are also updates to the project dependencies and minor refactoring for clarity and maintainability.

**Archive Integrity and Verification:**
- Added a streaming integrity check for chunked tar archives via the new `_ChainReader` and `verify_tar_parts_stream` in `archive_chunks.py`, allowing validation of multi-part archives without assembling them into a single file.
- Implemented `verify_uploaded_part_size` in `activescale.py` to confirm that uploaded S3 objects match expected sizes, improving reliability of uploads.

**S3 Object Retention and Configuration:**
- Added `set_object_retention` to `activescale.py` and corresponding settings in `config.py` to enable S3 Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode, with support for environment-based retention overrides for test environments. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5fa103311ec32fd86089f51043977396b7b3a7b36eca17a80a5a54a297840895R524-R648) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24a3fe5c783755412cb9de83238b4dfd0699345bf50dcadc3ec23c6749361592R66-R73)
- Updated `.env.development` to allow overriding S3 retention period for test environments.

**Dependency and Workflow Updates:**
- Upgraded `fastapi` dependency from `0.136.3` to `0.137.1` in `pyproject.toml`, and added a `dev` script for easier development. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L11-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R83)

**Refactoring and Minor Improvements:**
- Refactored retrieval worker to remove `asyncio` usage in favor of synchronous `time.sleep`, simplifying the code and avoiding unnecessary async complexity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4bcab20d5d75e405b1a9524448949ec2080e8e84bbf06be19f155ef49446723bL5-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4bcab20d5d75e405b1a9524448949ec2080e8e84bbf06be19f155ef49446723bL73-R73) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4bcab20d5d75e405b1a9524448949ec2080e8e84bbf06be19f155ef49446723bL88-L91) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4bcab20d5d75e405b1a9524448949ec2080e8e84bbf06be19f155ef49446723bL186-R182) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4bcab20d5d75e405b1a9524448949ec2080e8e84bbf06be19f155ef49446723bL255-R251)

author: ashutoshojha-odin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #787.

This PR hardens the packaged desktop Shogo IDE launch path so the macOS `.app` can open Shogo IDE reliably outside a developer shell. It addresses the production-only failures seen when launching from `out/Shogo-darwin-arm64/Shogo.app` with a restricted PATH and packaged resources.

The fix covers three related failure modes:

1. Packaged Shogo IDE setup could fail because `bun` was resolved from ambient PATH instead of from the packaged app bundle.
2. The packaged main process could fail because `dist/fs-ipc.js` still contained an unresolved workspace-source require for `@shogo/agent-runtime/src/fs-tree-walker`.
3. The IDE launch window could show `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` for `https://nodejs.org.../?folder=...` because the launcher accepted the first URL in process output instead of filtering for the local Code OSS server URL.

## Detailed changes

### Package Shogo IDE resources deterministically

- Adds `apps/desktop/scripts/sync-shogo-ide.mjs` to copy the Shogo IDE distribution assets into `apps/desktop/resources/apps/shogo-ide` before packaging.
- Adds `apps/desktop/scripts/run-sync-shogo-ide.mjs` as a CommonJS-compatible wrapper for Forge hooks.
- Updates `forge.config.ts` so `prePackage` runs the desktop build, web resource sync, and Shogo IDE resource sync before Forge captures the app bundle.
- Ensures stale desktop `dist/` output is not accidentally packaged.

### Use packaged Bun for Shogo IDE setup

- Updates `apps/desktop/src/shogo-ide.ts` to resolve the bundled Bun binary from app resources when packaged.
- Uses packaged Bun when running Shogo IDE materialization instead of assuming `bun` exists on PATH.
- Keeps development behavior intact by continuing to work against source/workspace paths when not packaged.

### Bundle all desktop main-process entrypoints that need workspace-source imports

- Updates `apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-main.mjs` to bundle both:
  - `src/main.ts -> dist/main.js`
  - `src/fs-ipc.ts -> dist/fs-ipc.js`
- Adds post-bundle validation to reject leaked build-host paths or unresolved workspace-source imports such as:
  - `@shogo/agent-runtime/src/...`
  - `@shogo-ai/worker/src/...`
- This prevents the packaged app from requiring source files that do not exist inside `app.asar`.

### Restrict Shogo IDE URL resolution to local server URLs

- Updates `apps/desktop/src/ide-views.ts` to parse process output through a dedicated local-server URL filter.
- Only accepts local Code OSS server hosts:
  - `127.0.0.1`
  - `localhost`
  - `::1`
  - `0.0.0.0`, normalized to `127.0.0.1`
- Ignores unrelated URLs emitted by Node.js/Code OSS startup output, including `https://nodejs.org...` help URLs.
- Prevents the false `Could not open Shogo IDE` dialog where the IDE process opens but the desktop app loads the wrong URL.

### Add packaged-app integrity checks

- Adds `apps/desktop/scripts/assert-packaged-shogo-ide.mjs`.
- Adds `npm run test:packaged-shogo-ide`.
- The check verifies the packaged `.app` contains:
  - bundled Bun,
  - Shogo IDE resources,
  - generated distribution metadata/materialization support,
  - no unresolved workspace-source requires in packaged JS.

### Extend Forge/package regression tests

- Updates `apps/desktop/test-forge-config.ts` to cover:
  - Shogo IDE resource sync hooks,
  - packaged Bun path expectations,
  - bundled `fs-ipc` expectations,
  - package integrity script wiring,
  - localhost-only IDE URL extraction.

## User impact

Before this PR, a user opening Shogo IDE from the packaged desktop app could encounter one or more of:

```text
bun run distribution:materialize exited with code 1
Cannot find module @shogo/agent-runtime/src/fs-tree-walker
Could not open Shogo IDE
ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED (-105) loading https://nodejs.org.../?folder=...
```

After this PR, the packaged app has a self-contained launch path:

- Shogo IDE resources are present in the app bundle.
- The app uses the bundled Bun binary for setup/materialization.
- Main-process workspace imports are bundled into packaged JS.
- URL detection ignores external documentation/help URLs and opens only the local IDE server.

## Verification

Ran locally from `apps/desktop`:

```bash
bun test-forge-config.ts
npm run build
npm run package
npm run test:packaged-shogo-ide
```

All checks passed.

Additional manual/targeted verification performed while debugging:

- Launched the packaged `.app` with a restricted production-like PATH (`/usr/bin:/bin`) to ensure it no longer depends on developer shell PATH for Bun.
- Simulated Shogo IDE materialization by copying packaged resources to a temporary directory and running `distribution:materialize` with the packaged Bun binary.
- Inspected packaged `app.asar` to verify the new localhost-only Code OSS URL extraction logic was present.

## Notes

Generated packaging artifacts such as `apps/desktop/resources/mcp-packages/`, `apps/desktop/resources/ms-playwright/`, and `apps/desktop/resources/sdk-cli.mjs` were intentionally not committed. They are build/package outputs rather than source changes.

author: hiq-lab
body:
## Summary

`ArvakProvider.get_backend('ibm_*')` now routes through the native
Rust `arvak-adapter-ibm` via PyO3. Replaces the in-Python `requests`
HTTP loop in `ArvakIBMBackend`.

Both US-East (`IBM_SERVICE_CRN`) and EU Frankfurt (`IBM_SERVICE_CRN_EU`)
regions are supported with the same env-var conventions the legacy
class used. The native adapter eagerly fetches real backend topology
and qubit count from the IBM Cloud API on construction — no more
127-qubit `conservative fallback`.

qrisp has no IBM bypass (its `_HARDWARE_BACKENDS` is only `{iqm,
scaleway}`), so no cross-integration sweep — RFC §Phase 4 impact map
shows `n/a` for cirq/pennylane/qrisp on IBM.

## Hidden-behaviour audit (RFC §Risks #2)

The legacy class had two hardcoded values worth flagging:

1. **`max_qubits = 127  # conservative fallback`** — used when live
   backend-info HTTP fetch failed. Native adapter avoids: `connect()`
   fetches real `num_qubits` at construction, no silent fallback.
2. **27-qubit hardcoded heavy-hex topology** — was a test fixture in
   `_BACKEND_INFO_CACHE` for `ibm_torino`. Native adapter queries
   IBM Cloud for the real topology.

Both are improvements, not regressions. Documented in commit for
Phase-7 cleanup.

## What changed

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| **Cargo feature** | New `adapter-ibm`, in `default` |
| **`make_backend()`** | Prefix branch for `ibm_*` (8 US + 3 EU). EU backends shim `IBM_SERVICE_CRN_EU` into the adapter's `IBM_SERVICE_CRN` read. Calls async `IbmBackend::connect()` via shared tokio runtime |
| **`known_backends()`** | Lists all 11 IBM machines |
| **qiskit `ArvakProvider`** | `ibm_*` lookups return `ArvakBackend` (native) instead of `ArvakIBMBackend` (legacy) |
| **`ArvakIBMBackend`** | Importable, emits `DeprecationWarning` at construction |
| **qrisp** | No change — has no IBM bypass to fix |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all` clean
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --exclude arvak-python` green
- [x] `cargo test -p arvak-python --lib backend::`: 6 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p arvak-adapter-ibm --lib`: 42 passed (no regression)
- [x] 52/52 pre-existing qiskit + circuit tests pass
- [x] 13 Phase-1.5, 10 Phase-2a, 10 Phase-2b, 11 Phase-3 smoke tests: all pass
- [x] 11 new Phase-4 smoke tests cover:
  - registry lists 11 IBM backends (8 US + 3 EU)
  - clear error for missing `IBM_API_KEY` / `IBM_SERVICE_CRN`
  - EU-specific error mentions `IBM_SERVICE_CRN_EU`
  - EU CRN env-var override accepted (passes validation)
  - `ArvakProvider` routes via `ArvakBackend`
  - legacy class emits `DeprecationWarning`
  - qrisp confirmed no IBM bypass (nothing else to fix)
  - sim / iqm_garnet / scaleway_garnet unchanged
- [ ] CI: this PR's run

## No live IBM Cloud calls in tests

Per the project memory rule. Construction with dummy credentials
would hit IBM Cloud auth and fail — only env-var error paths,
deprecation, and routing assertions covered.

## Out of scope

- **YAQS evaluation** for IBM noise modelling — opted to skip per
  user "weiter" (RFC gate is explicit non-blocking).
- **Token-mode fallback** (`IBM_QUANTUM_TOKEN` without API key) —
  native adapter supports it via `IbmBackend::with_target()` but
  not wired in registry; can be added later if anyone uses the
  legacy path.

author: spjmurray
body:
The region API server serves single-resource GETs and Lists from the
controller-runtime cache, which is repopulated asynchronously by a watch.
Writes are synchronous to the apiserver, so an immediate read-back after a
create or update races the cache and can observe the pre-write object (a
stale name/spec, or a resource not yet present in a list).

This caused the networks "should reflect updated name and description"
spec to flake: the PUT response correctly echoed the updated name, but the
immediate round-trip GET returned the pre-update name.

Wrap every immediate read-back of a just-written resource in a bounded
Eventually (5s timeout, 250ms polling), matching the existing convention in
the load balancer and security group suites. The PUT/POST response
assertions remain immediate and authoritative; only the cache-backed
re-reads tolerate convergence.

---
Fresh PR for the built-in recorder work (supersedes the previous one).

Includes everything verified green across all ABIs in CI:

## 1. On-demand GPU tee (zero idle overhead)
Native Minecraft renders straight to the display when idle; the recorder only borrows the surface while recording. Encoder priority/operating-rate tuning + URGENT_DISPLAY GL thread. Safe revert if the surface hand-off fails (gameplay never harmed).

## 2. Game-audio capture (OpenAL mixer inline-hook, route b)
Inline-hook OpenAL-soft's `ALCdevice::renderSamples` via **ShadowHook** (UNIQUE mode), resolving the LOCAL symbol from `.symtab`. Final mixed 16-bit PCM is copied into a lock-free ring buffer, drained by a pump thread into a hardware **AAC** encoder, and muxed as a 2nd MP4 track with PTS anchored to a common start. Captures game sounds + simple-voicechat playback, no MediaProjection / permission prompt. Falls back to video-only if the tap is unavailable.

ShadowHook ships arm only, so its prebuilt `.so` + header are **vendored** under `jni/recordzytap/{prebuilt,include}` and linked via `PREBUILT_SHARED_LIBRARY` gated on arm ABIs (x86/x86_64 build clean, video-only).

## 3. On-screen diagnostics
No-logcat-needed toasts on start/stop showing audio status, the hooked-call count, and captured-sample count, plus native status codes - so we can pin down any 'no audio' cause directly on device.

## Testing
- CI: all ABI debug builds pass (arm64, arm, x86, x86_64, all).
- **Needs on-device testing** on the Snapdragon 7s Gen 2: confirm the start toast reports audio, that it's in sync, and watch for hitches. The toasts report the exact failure reason if audio doesn't engage.

## Summary

- Adds `postinstall: prisma generate` to `package.json` so Vercel generates the Prisma client before building
- Creates `src/types/prisma-enums.ts` with plain TypeScript const mirrors of all Prisma enums, eliminating `@prisma/client` imports from client components entirely
- Updates all affected client components (`appointment-slide-over`, `appointments-filters`, `appointment-status-badge`, `customer-activity`, `customer-conversations`, `conversation-list-item`, `thread-header`) to import from the new enums file
- Also includes Phase 4A messaging inbound rewrite and notification jobs API route

## Root cause

Turbopack bundles client components for the browser. When a client component imports from `@prisma/client`, Turbopack tries to resolve `index-browser.js → .prisma/client/index-browser`, which only exists after `prisma generate` runs. On Vercel, `node_modules` is rebuilt from scratch on each deploy without running `prisma generate`, so the file is never there.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger a Vercel deploy after merging — build should complete without the `Can't resolve '.prisma/client/index-browser'` error
- [ ] Verify appointments, inbox, and customer pages render correctly in production

author: baileypodcast
body:
## What

The weekly Salesforce reconcile (`/import`) had no way to clear an uploaded import and its proposed change list. The page always rendered the latest run, so a wrong or stale upload was stuck on screen with no escape hatch.

This adds a **"Discard this import"** button next to the last-run indicator in the upload section.

## How

- `clearSyncRun(runId)` in `lib/salesforce/sync.ts` deletes the run. The `salesforce_sync_flags.run_id` FK is `on delete cascade` (db/120), so the proposed change list clears with it and the page falls back to the empty upload state. It also deletes the run's `salesforce_conflict` Today alert so a discarded import stops nagging.
- `clearRunAction()` server action in `app/(dashboard)/import/sync-actions.ts`, gated on the same `import` edit permission as the rest of the reconcile.
- `WeeklyReconcile` gets a confirm-guarded button wired to the action.

## Safety

- **Already-applied changes are preserved.** `sync_audit_log.run_id` is `on delete set null`, so the audit trail survives the discard, and guest writes are never touched — this only clears the *pending review list*, not history.
- The confirm dialog spells this out before deleting.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean across the project.
- Could not exercise the live Supabase delete from this environment; the cascade/null behaviour is read directly from the committed `db/120` schema.

author: ivanbelyakoff
body:
Implements **RD-1137 Part B** — the unconditional half the CTO approved ("denial reason must reach the admin logs panel in any case"). The opt-in **verbose-error-on-the-wire** half (Part A, group-flag-gated) is a separate follow-up.

> ⚠️ **Stacked on #330 (RD-1135).** Base is the RD-1135 branch so this diff shows only Part-B changes. Rebase to `main` after #330 merges.

## Problem
The access log records only the status code. The real denial reason lives in **slog/stdout** (operator-only — org admins can't query it), and trace denials are logged as a **hardcoded 403** regardless of the real status. So in the (now org-scoped, RD-1135) Access Logs panel an admin sees *that* a request failed, not *why* — the worked example `call denied: invalid request shape` was really "sender address not linked."

## What this does
- **Migration 062:** `access_logs.denial_reason TEXT NULL`. **Not** part of the `entry_hash` (chain + verifier untouched, `hash_format_version` stays 2 — same posture as `org_id`/061). No backfill.
- **Curated reason taxonomy** (`internal/server/denial_reasons.go`): stable, tenant-safe codes — `sender_not_linked`, `method_not_allowed`, `cross_org`, `invalid_request_shape`, `tracing_unavailable`, `trace_depth_exceeded`, `auth_required`, … Never raw error text.
- **`ProcessError.Reason` + `ProcessRequest.denialReason`**, threaded into the access-log writers (stored, not hashed). Every **logged** denial is classified across the eth_call/estimateGas, eth_sendTransaction, eth_sendRawTransaction (+ deploy) trace paths and the RBAC entry-point deny.
- **Fixes the hardcoded-403 mislabel:** trace-deny call sites now log the real `StatusCode` (e.g. 400 for `invalid_request_shape`).
- **Surfaces it:** `GET /api/v1/admin/logs` returns `denial_reason`; the dashboard Access Logs view gains a humanized **Reason** column.

## Security
The reason is **opaque on the wire** in this PR — it only lands in the access-log row, shown in the **org-scoped** admin view (RD-1135). `cross_org` and other oracle-sensitive codes are stored precisely for the admin view; Part A's wire exposure is what will apply the oracle-collapse before any code reaches an external caller.

## Testing
- `go test ./internal/server/ ./internal/db/` green.
- New: denial reason round-trips through `/logs` and is omitted for success; `logAccess` forwards the reason; hash-chain verifier still passes with the column populated.

## Not classified (NULL — noted follow-ups)
Rate-limit (429) / upstream (502) — status already conveys these; `debug_trace` denials; compliance denials aren't routed through `logAccess` today (separate gap).

author: andresgutgon
body:
## Problem

A **401 `UnauthorizedError`** thrown when accessing a sandbox without a valid session was being reported to **Datadog Error Tracking** as if it were a server fault ([monitor issue `d8e806a8-659b-11f1-8841-da7ad0900005`](https://app.datadoghq.eu/error-tracking?query=service%3A%2A&sp=%5B%7B%22p%22%3A%7B%22issueId%22%3A%22d8e806a8-659b-11f1-8841-da7ad0900005%22%7D%2C%22i%22%3A%22error-tracking-issue%22%7D%5D), service `web`).

> Note: `@issue.id` is not a searchable facet in this org's index, so the issue was located by signature rather than id. The matching error surfaces in spans as `error.type: Error` with message `{"_tag":"UnauthorizedError","message":"Unauthorized","status":401}` on `GET` request spans (e.g. a page SSR load whose loader calls `assertAuthenticatedSession`).

## Root cause

The web tracing middleware in `apps/web/src/start.ts` recorded **every** thrown error to Datadog via `recordSpanExceptionForDatadog`, regardless of HTTP status, at **two** sites:

- `tracingFnMiddleware` records the *original* error on the **server-fn span** (resource = fn name, e.g. `annotations.listTraceAnnotations`).
- `tracingRequestMiddleware` records the *re-thrown payload* `Error` on the **request span** (resource `GET`) — and that re-thrown error is a plain `Error`, so it wasn't even classifiable by status.

So caller-driven 4xx (a 401 with no session, 404s, `ValidationError` 400s) opened Error Tracking issues and buried real 5xx bugs.

## Fix

Gate both recording sites on status — a 4xx means the caller was rejected as designed (expected control flow), not a server fault:

- Shared `isExpectedClientError(status)` classifier (400–499).
- `recordServerFnError` (fn middleware): skips `recordException`/`ERROR` status for 4xx, and stamps the re-thrown `Error` with **non-enumerable** `httpStatus`/`httpMessage` so it stays classifiable downstream **without** leaking into the client-bound JSON message.
- `recordRequestError` (request middleware): skips recording for 4xx; records `>=500` and non-HTTP (treated as 500) exactly as before.

4xx still carry `http.status_code` on the span, so they remain queryable in APM — they're only excluded from Error Tracking.

### Coverage / scope
This also clears sibling 4xx noise (e.g. `Too big/Too small: expected string…` and `Name cannot be empty` `ValidationError`s, `You are not the recipient…`, `…sign up is not enabled`) while **keeping** genuine faults like `Repository query failed: column "source" does not exist` (a real 500), `ECONNRESET` (infra) and Framer upstream failures.

Out of scope: `handler /…` spans (Better Auth / Nitro route handlers) and `client.error` spans (browser RUM) are produced by different instrumentation, so their 4xx are not affected by this change — possible follow-up.

## Tests
`apps/web/src/start.test.ts` (new) covers both helpers: 401/404 not recorded, 5xx/unknown recorded, the re-thrown error stays `isHttpError`-classifiable without leaking `httpStatus` into its JSON message, and the **end-to-end** path (server-fn 401 → re-thrown → request middleware also leaves it unrecorded). Verified the tests fail without the gate (both directions) and pass with it.

- `pnpm --filter web test` — 43 suites / 494 pass
- `pnpm --filter web typecheck` (tsgo) clean; `biome check` clean

## Verification after deploy
Occurrences of issue `d8e806a8…` (and the related 4xx issues above) should drop to zero. Real 5xx issues continue to report.

author: gytxxsy
body: ## Description Fix a memory leak in `mdns_priv_query_result_add_txt()` when `search->num_results >= search->max_results`. ### Root Cause When a TXT response was parsed, memory for `txt`, `txt_value_len`, and TXT key/value strings was already allocated. If the query result list was full (`num_results == max_results`), the function returned without attaching the new result and without freeing the allocated TXT buffers. ### Fix Return immediately only after successful insertion into result list. For full-list cases, fall through to `free_txt` and release all allocated TXT buffers. --- ## Checklist Before submitting a Pull Request, please ensure the following: - [x] 🚨 This PR does not introduce breaking changes. - [ ] All CI checks (GH Actions) pass. - [ ] ~Documentation is updated as needed.~ - [ ] ~Tests are updated or added as necessary.~ - [ ] ~Code is well-commented, especially in complex areas.~ - [x] Git history is clean — commits are squashed to the minimum necessary. --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Single control-flow change in mDNS querier cleanup path; no API or behavior change beyond fixing a leak when result limits are hit. > > **Overview** > Fixes a memory leak in **`mdns_priv_query_result_add_txt()`** when an mDNS search already has **`num_results >= max_results`**. > > Parsed TXT buffers (`txt`, `txt_value_len`, and key/value strings) were allocated before the function decided whether to attach them. A **`return`** after the “room for another result” branch ran on the full-list path too, so those buffers were never released. > > The change **returns only after a successful attach** (existing result updated or new `mdns_result_t` linked). When the cap blocks a new entry, execution **falls through to `free_txt`** and frees the orphaned TXT memory. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f81720b78c6bbfa12553db58be232bb8c37d57a0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

author: naninu123
body:
## Problem

During rolling node restarts or scale-down events, the proxy's graceful shutdown sequence drains active connections with a 30-second deadline. When the timeout expires while connections are still active, they become **zombie connections**: TCP state is closed on the proxy side but the client and upstream maintain their connection state, causing ghost entries in the flow table.

## Changes

### Two-Phase Shutdown (`graceful-shutdown.rs`)
- Phase 1 (0-25s): stops accepting new connections, sends HTTP/2 GOAWAY
- Phase 2 (25-30s): sends TCP RST to remaining connections instead of FIN
- Atomic phase tracking via `ShutdownPhase` enum

### Connection Migration (`connection-drainer.ts`)
- Per-connection drain orchestration with migration tokens for WebSocket/HTTP/2
- Phase-aware teardown: GOAWAY in phase 1, RST/destroy in phase 2

### Stale-Entry TTL + Socket-Close Callback (`flow-table.rs`)
- Configurable 60s stale-entry TTL eviction
- Immediate eviction via `on_socket_close()` callback
- Phase 2 orphan sweep via `evict_orphans()`

### Connection Monitoring (`connection-tracker.ts`)
- Real-time active connection counter with threshold events
- Drain/force-close tracking

### Lifecycle Manager (`lifecycle-manager.rs`)
- Health/liveness/readiness probes coordinated across subsystems
- 15s startup grace period before declaring readiness
- Shutdown coordination entry-point

### Zombie Detection (`zombie-detector.ts`)
- Periodic TCP keepalive probes for orphaned flow entries
- Eviction on timeout or RST response (both mean connection is dead)
- Configurable scan interval (default 60s)

## Metrics & Verification
- Connections drained vs. force-closed tracked per shutdown event
- Zombie count post-shutdown reported (target: 0)
- Full unit test coverage on all Rust modules

Closes #17

author: shilei-massclouds
body:
## Problem

  Running StarryOS tests with `lockdep` enabled exposed several lock-order issues:

  - Fork/clone address-space duplication takes the source AddrSpace lock and then the newly created AddrSpace lock, but this  structured nesting was not annotated.
  - Futex requeue/wait paths can take nested wait queue locks, which lockdep may classify as same-class recursive locking
  without an explicit subclass.
  - `ax-fs-ng` cached reads held cached-file locks while writing into the destination buffer. If that buffer points to user
  memory, the copy can fault and acquire AddrSpace, creating a cached I/O/page cache -> AddrSpace edge.
  - The ax-fs-ng block runtime repoll path could keep the pending lock held across repoll, creating unnecessary lock-order
  risk.

  ## Changes

  - Annotate cloned AddrSpace locking with a nested lock subclass.
  - Annotate nested futex wait queue locking with a nested lock subclass.
  - Narrow `CachedFile::read_at()` locking so cached data is copied into a scratch page while holding cached-file locks, then
  copied to the destination after releasing them.
  - Release the ax-fs-ng block runtime pending lock before repolling.

author: dhkun
body:
## 改动内容

- 为 grdp 的 TPKT、X224、MCS、SEC 和 PDU 事件层安装 panic 回收器
- 将子 goroutine panic 转换为普通 RDP 登录错误
- 为 TCP 连接设置覆盖完整握手过程的 deadline
- 使用单次完成通道收敛 error、close、success、ready 和 panic 路径
- 移除 RDP 扫描结束阶段的忙循环
- 添加事件 panic 回归测试、单次完成测试和本地挂起服务超时测试

## 根因

`grdp` 的事件监听器在子 goroutine 中执行。异常 NLA 响应会让 `TPKT.recvChallenge` 访问空的 `NegoTokens[0]`，panic 跨越 goroutine 边界，现有 `ScanFunc` 外层 `recover` 无法捕获。

RDP 登录流程使用无限 `WaitGroup` 等待，扫描结束使用 `for !signal {}` 忙循环。异常协议路径会导致进程终止、流程卡住或持续占用 CPU。

## 用户影响

畸形或异常 RDP 响应会返回可记录的错误，dddd 扫描进程继续运行。单次凭据尝试受到统一超时控制。

## 验证

- `go test ./gopocs -run 'TestRDP' -count=5 -timeout=30s`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `go build ./...`

Closes #3

body:
# Description

Merges the MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration into develop, enabling AI agents to discover and invoke Imagify abilities via the WordPress MCP adapter.

Implements the complete epic #1097 "As an AI agent, I want Imagify to expose MCP abilities" with all 7 core abilities and the MCP foundation.

**User Impact:** AI agents can now:
- Discover Imagify capabilities via the `/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server` endpoint
- Optimize media attachments on demand
- Retrieve account status, settings, media status, and optimization statistics
- Update Imagify configuration settings
- Generate missing next-gen image versions
- Restore original media files

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #(issue number)
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

- All 7 MCP abilities registered and functional via REST endpoint
- Ability metadata discoverable via `discover-abilities` tool
- Individual ability info retrievable via `get-ability-info` tool
- Ability execution via `execute-ability` tool
- Permission checks enforced (`manage_options` capability)
- Integration tests for ability registration and permission validation
- Playwright E2E tests for UI interaction flows

### How to test

1. Ensure WordPress 6.9+ (Abilities API required)
2. Activate the Imagify plugin
3. Verify the MCP endpoint: `GET /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server`
4. Expected: endpoint returns ability metadata for all 7 abilities
5. Run: `npm test` (integration & unit tests)
6. Run: `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright scenarios)

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

**New modules:** MCP server, abilities infrastructure (ConfigSubscriber, AbilitiesSubscriber, ServiceProvider)

**Affected existing modules:** None directly—MCP integration is isolated to a new module under `classes/MCP/` and new ability classes under `classes/Abilities/`. No changes to existing optimization, media handling, or settings logic.

**QA scope:** MCP endpoint functionality, ability discovery, permission validation, API input/output contracts.

## Technical description

### Documentation

See `docs/api/mcp.md` for full MCP module documentation, including:
- Boot flow and requirements (WP 6.9+)
- REST endpoint contract
- AbilitiesInterface implementation guide
- Individual ability specifications (input/output schemas, error codes)
- How to add new abilities

### Architecture

**New classes:**
- `Imagify\MCP\ServiceProvider` — DI wiring for MCP services
- `Imagify\MCP\ConfigSubscriber` — Customizes MCP server name/description
- `Imagify\MCP\AbilitiesSubscriber` — Registers ability category and injects abilities
- `Imagify\Abilities\AbilitiesInterface` — Contract for all abilities
- `Imagify\Abilities\*` — 7 concrete ability implementations

**Integration points:**
- Hooked on `plugins_loaded` → `imagify_init()` → boots `McpAdapter::instance()`
- Listens to `mcp_adapter_default_server_config`, `wp_abilities_api_categories_init`, `wp_abilities_api_init` actions
- Registered in DI container via `config/providers.php`

### New dependencies

- `wordpress/mcp-adapter ^0.5.0` (composer dependency, already declared)

### Risks

**Security:** All abilities check `manage_options` capability. No public-facing data leaks.

**Performance:** Abilities are lazy-loaded via DI container. No runtime overhead unless MCP endpoint is called.

**Compatibility:** Guarded by `function_exists()` checks for Abilities API. No-ops silently on WP < 6.9.

**Mitigation:** Integration tests validate permission checks; E2E tests confirm happy paths.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] All acceptance criteria validated (7 abilities functional, endpoint discoverable)
- [x] Triggered all changed code paths via automated tests
- [x] Integrated test coverage for ability registration, permission checks, input validation

## Code style

- [x] Self-explanatory code with clear responsibility separation
- [x] Input validation and permission checks at all entry points
- [x] No unnecessary abstraction; follows BackWPup MCP pattern
- [x] Error messages are explicit with actionable error codes (`imagify_unknown_setting`, `imagify_invalid_value`, etc.)

## Unticked items justification

N/A — all mandatory items addressed.

# Additional Checks

- [x] Complex code paths documented in `docs/api/mcp.md`
- [x] Ability execution results logged via standard WordPress filters (`wp_abilities_api_init` logging available)
- [x] Error handling for invalid inputs, API key immutability, constrained field validation

author: mpecan
body:
## Why

An audit of the surfaces consumers actually plug into — the embed core's options/handles/sinks and the extension's buttons — ahead of store release, while there are no external consumers to break. The audit found the pluggable API inconsistent and under-exposed, and the buttons stylistically consistent but structurally fragmented (no shared component, duplicated arrays/CSS). This applies the improvements.

## What changed

### Pluggable API (`src/embed`)
- **`ExportSink` is now first-class.** `MountOptions` takes `sink?` (plug your own delivery — server POST, FileSystem, retries) **or** `onExport?` (wrapped in `BindingSink`); `mount()` requires one, `sink` wins. Previously embedders only got a callback.
- **Injectable storage** via a named `StorageAdapter` port + `createInMemoryStorage()` (default) / `createLocalStorageStorage()` (persists the changelog across reloads).
- **Named `ScreenshotProvider`** type; the public types/factories (`ExportSink`/`StorageAdapter`/`ScreenshotProvider`, `BindingSink`, storage factories) are re-exported from `src/embed`.
- **Real version** baked via a build-time `__STM_VERSION__` define (replaces the hardcoded `0.0.0-embed`), read lazily in `getVersion` so the extension — which imports the barrel without that define — doesn't trip a load-time `ReferenceError`.

### Buttons / shared UI (`src/ui`)
- New shared **`Button`** (`primary`/`secondary`/`ghost`) + `controls.css` (`.stm-btn`), `@import`ed into both the pages and the panel shadow root; adopted across popup, options, and the panel footer/agent actions — no more per-surface button classes.
- **`useCopy`** hook dedupes the Copy→Copied logic; **`TOOL_KINDS`/`DRAWING_TOOLS`** in `src/core/model` replace the duplicated tool arrays (Options default-tool now correctly excludes `select`).
- **Light palettes reconciled:** the panel now uses beige bg / white surface to match the pages.

### Docs
- `CLAUDE.md` + `SPEC.md` §13 updated to match the as-built API.

## Breaking changes (pre-release, no external consumers)
- `WidgetConfig.onSubmit` → `onExport`
- Channel-A `EmbedHandle.triggerExport` → `exportNow` (matches the in-page `StmHandle.exportNow`)
- `MountOptions.onExport` is now optional (provide `sink` or `onExport`)

## Verification
All §8 gates green: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` (zero warnings), `pnpm test` (coverage thresholds incl. `src/core` 100%), `pnpm build` + `build:firefox`, `pnpm size`, `pnpm check:perms`, full `pnpm e2e` (extension + Channel A/B), and `pnpm e2e:cli` (Channel C). Panel light-theme reconciliation verified in a headless browser. A `/simplify` pass followed the implementation (deduped the widget delivery-wrapper, migrated the last copy button to `Button`, reduced `.popup__link` to the ghost variant).

## Follow-ups (deliberately not in this PR)
- A token-parity guard test asserting the `theme.css` ↔ `panel.css` palettes stay in sync (the one hand-sync invariant left unguarded — the selector-scope constraint, `:root` vs `.stm-panel`, prevents a single `@import`-able token source).

author: josephnef
body:
Implements the actual decode behind the Phase-4 VHT extension seams, plus the two fixes that make real over-the-air HT/VHT frames decode.

## What
- VHT SU SISO (MCS 0-7, 20 MHz, BCC): VHT-SIG-A (BPSK+QBPSK) + VHT-SIG-B length + VHT data.
- HT-SIG two-axis decode (real Realtek = BPSK pilots + QBPSK data on the imag axis; try real then eq*-j).
- HT STBC (Alamouti) and 2x2 MIMO (MCS 8-15) data paths.
- HT/VHT LDPC (fec==1) via a new header-only min-sum decoder (ldpc_min_sum.h).
- HT-LTF channel estimate for HT20/HT40 data tones.

## Over-air fixes (the headline)
1. sync_short MIN_GAP 480 -> 700: an HT-mixed/VHT frame has a second short-training field (HT-STF) at L-STF+560 samples; the old gap re-triggered a spurious frame start mid-packet, mis-windowing every HT/VHT frame. Legacy (no HT-STF) was unaffected -- why HT/VHT got 0 over-air decodes while legacy worked.
2. equalize_ht_sig drops the SDR-invalid sampling ramp (eps0=CFO/f_carrier assumes a shared TX/RX oscillator; false for SDR capture of an independent transmitter).

## Validation
- Synthetic regression green: legacy/HT20/HT20-spec/HT40/VHT20/STBC/LDPC; MIMO --selftest bit-exact.
- Over-air (RTL8812AU TX -> B210 -> blind decode, ch149): HT MCS0 (238), HT MCS4 (956), VHT MCS0 (240), VHT MCS4 (955) all decode to the expected MCS.

## Summary
Adds `OrderPlacedHandler`, a MediatR handler for the existing `OrderCreatedEvent` that fans out to the admin SignalR alert (`NotifyOrderPlacedAsync` → `AdminsGroup`, `type: order-placed`) and the ops email (`SendNewOrderEmailAsync`). Each side-effect is failure-isolated so a push/email error never rolls back order placement (events dispatch pre-commit).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `OrderPlacedHandler` implements `INotificationHandler<OrderCreatedEvent>`, loads the order (+user) via `IReadDbContext`, fans out to `IPaymentNotifier.NotifyOrderPlacedAsync` and `IEmailService.SendNewOrderEmailAsync`; auto-registered by the existing MediatR assembly scan.

- [x] `IPaymentNotifier` gains `NotifyOrderPlacedAsync`; `PaymentSignalRNotifier` broadcasts to `PaymentHub.AdminsGroup` on `ReceivePaymentNotification` with type `order-placed` carrying orderId, orderNumber (SlugId), placedAt (CreatedAt), total, itemCount, timestamp.

Place an order with an admin connected to the dashboard SignalR feed → confirm an `order-placed` push reaches the admins group and an email is sent to `Email:OpsRecipient`. Force the email/push to throw (e.g. bad config) → confirm the order still persists and the other side-effect still fires.

body:
💡 What: Optimized the rendering performance of the `FlatList` in `app/(tabs)/home.tsx` by hoisting pure helper functions (`formatIncidentDate`, `parseMediaUrls`, `openIncidentMap`) outside the functional component, wrapping `openIncidentDetails` and the inline `onEndReached` handler in `useCallback`, and wrapping the `renderIncidentItem` itself in `useCallback`.

🎯 Why: In React Native, inline functions and unmemoized callbacks passed to components like `FlatList` cause unnecessary function allocations on every render and trigger continuous re-renders of the list items as the user scrolls, leading to frame drops and high garbage collection overhead.

📊 Impact: Reduces memory allocation and avoids unnecessary re-renders of `FlatList` items when the `Home` component's state changes (e.g., when syncing or loading more data).

🔬 Measurement: Profile the application using the React DevTools Profiler or the React Native Performance monitor while scrolling the "Incidents Terrain" list and observing the reduction in component re-render times.

body:
Two small, independent hardening/quality items from the code-review sweep.

## Dockerfile — run as a non-root user (defence-in-depth)
The container previously ran as `root`. Adds an unprivileged `aggregator`
system user that owns `/app` (so `uv run` can use its venv/cache and the app can
write the `/app/data` store and logs), and switches to it before `CMD`. A
freshly-created `equity_data` named volume inherits this ownership on first mount.

**Note for existing deployments:** a pre-existing `equity_data` volume created
under earlier root runs stays root-owned; it would need recreating (or a one-off
`chown`) once. Fresh `docker compose up` is unaffected.

## Logging — standardise on lazy `%`-style + enforce with ruff `G`
- Converts the three eager f-string log calls in `exchange_rate_api.py` to lazy
  `%`-style, matching the ~66 existing calls.
- Enables ruff's `G` (flake8-logging-format) rule so f-string logging is caught
  going forward.
- `G` additionally flagged five `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` calls (xetra,
  gleif ×2, resolve); these are converted to the idiomatic `logger.exception(...)`
  (equivalent output, all inside `except` blocks).

## Verification
- `uv run ruff check src` — clean
- `uv run ruff format --check src` — clean
- `uv run pytest -m unit` — 1218 passed (100% coverage)
- Docker hardening needs a real build to fully verify filesystem permissions;
  not exercised in CI.

author: p13marc
body:
## Why
Demo mode (`--demo`) and the `zensight::mock` boot seed only knew about the four original sensors (sysinfo, snmp, modbus, syslog). Since then we added the **netlink**, **netring**, **netflow** and **gnmi** sensors and the sensor-emitted **`@/alerts`** channel — so under `--demo` their specialized views, the **Security/Anomalies** view, and the topology overlay all rendered empty.

I surveyed each real sensor's publishing code (5 parallel explorers) and replicated their exact telemetry contracts.

## What
- **netlink** — per-interface counters (`iface/<n>/rx_bytes` … with `ifindex` label), TCP socket-state gauges, route/neighbor inventory, rolled-up `diagnostics/*`, RTNETLINK `events/*` counters — one set per Linux host.
- **netring** — `flow/*` lifecycle & volume, per-L4 + TCP-teardown counters, `bandwidth/<app>/bytes_per_sec` (label `app`), TLS/DNS/HTTP RED rollups — one probe.
- **netflow** — one byte-counter series per `{src}/{dst}/{proto}` from an exporter, with `version`/`exporter_ip` labels.
- **gnmi** — streamed `interfaces/interface[name=…]/state/...` YANG paths.
- **Sensor alerts** — new security anomalies (port scan, beaconing → netring **Anomaly**; downed service → netlink **Expectation**) run through the scheduler and `generate_alerts()` with a correct **firing→resolved** lifecycle, yielded as `Message::AlertReceived`. Populates the Security view in demo.
- **Syslog fix** — demo emitted `message/<id>`, which the frontend parsed as facility=`message`, severity=Informational. Switched to the real `<facility>/<severity>` path; also fixed mock's `kern`/`err` slugs. Severity/facility filtering now works.
- **Health + liveness** extended to all eight sensors; demo subscription counts the new protocols.

## Tests
New unit tests: all protocols present in a tick, health covers every sensor, anomaly→alert mapping, firing/resolved lifecycle, syslog path format. `cargo test -p zensight` green (188/188; one pre-existing live-Zenoh test is flaky under parallel load — passes in isolation). `cargo fmt` clean.

body:
## What

모바일(폰)에서 **SkyStrip**(LIVE AQI 밴드 — Home·Today 상단 `LIVE / SEOUL·KR / PM2.5 … / p10–p90 / DQSS / n=stations / 좌표로 입력 / N STATIONS`)를 페이지 거터에 정렬. `apps/web/src/reado-dark.css`에 `@media (max-width: 480px)` 1블록 추가.

## Why — 가로 삼중 inset (실측)

iPhone(~390px)에서 SkyStrip 콘텐츠가 양쪽 **~64px씩** 들어가 content ≈262px로 매우 좁았다:

1. `.public-page-container[data-tier="hub"]` `padding-inline: var(--pad-x)` (~20px) — `reado.css:362`
2. `.reado-shell .sky-strip` `margin: 0 var(--pad-x)` (~20px) — `reado-dark.css:71`
3. `.reado-shell .sky-strip` `padding: 18px 24px` 가로 24px — `reado-dark.css:70`

② margin + ③ 가로 padding이 ① 페이지 거터 위에 **이중**으로 더해진 게 낭비. 사용자 결정 = **게터 정렬**: SkyStrip 자체 margin·가로 padding·좌우 border만 제거 → 표준 거터(~20px)만 남아 Masthead/Hero 등 본문과 정렬.

## Change

```css
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .reado-shell .sky-strip {
    margin-left: 0; margin-right: 0;
    padding-left: 0; padding-right: 0;
    border-left: 0; border-right: 0;
  }
}
```

- longhand만 → 세로 padding(18px)·상/하 border(밴드)·`overflow`·`data-aqi` 그라데이션 보존.
- `.reado-shell .sky-strip` 선택자 = base(`reado.css:515`, 특이도 0,1,0)와 dark의 `.reado-shell .sky-strip`(0,2,0) 둘 다 덮음. reado-dark.css가 reado.css보다 나중 import라 동일 특이도에서도 승리. `.sky-strip--expanded`(L85) **뒤** 배치 → 확장 변형도 거터 정렬(parity).
- Home·Today 동일 `.sky-strip` 공유 → 한 규칙이 정확히 두 면만 커버(다른 페이지는 SkyStrip 미사용).

## Scope / 5-guard

- **CSS-only 1파일 1블록** (`reado-dark.css`). 컴포넌트·마크업 변경 0.
- **Glass-box 불변** — p10–p90 / DQSS / n=stations 렌더 그대로(순수 spacing).
- 데스크탑(≥481px) 0 회귀 — `@media (max-width:480px)` only. `:root`/토큰 미변경.
- migration/secret/Edge Fn/billing 무관.

## Verification

author: totoseo
body:
## Context
Traffic just jumped (10 → 120 clicks/day) and several users left 1★ reviews over **"résultats complètement faussés."** I audited the scoring engine and the question/result data in all 5 languages (FR/EN/ES/DE/IT) and fixed the confirmed bugs, then added a retention feature. Everything below was verified by driving the real quizzes headless in Chromium.

## 🔴 Critical scoring bugs fixed

### 1. `couple-sain` (healthy) was fully **inverted** in EN/ES/DE/IT
The non-FR `healthy` questions are authored option **a = least healthy → d = healthiest**, but the engine scored them `a=3 … d=0`. Net effect across **312 questions (78 × 4 langs)**:
- A perfectly healthy couple scored **0% → "Foundations to (re)build"** (worst tier)
- A toxic couple scored **100% → "A fulfilling relationship"** (best tier)

Fix: reverse the weighting **only** for the native `healthy` prefix. FR uses the `couple` prefix (authored a=healthiest) and was already correct, so it's untouched. Also fixed a latent `usedPrefix` detection bug that returned `'healthy'` even in FR.

✅ Verified: picking the healthiest answers now yields the **top** tier at 100% in all 5 languages.

### 2. `distance` (FR) showed **no conclusion**
The engine reads `pv_*` / `cv_*` verdict keys, which existed only in non-FR. French users saw score rings but **blank verdict text**. Added French individual + couple verdicts (matched to the FR existing-relationship framing).

### 3. `distance` (EN/ES/DE/IT) showed a spurious **French 4th option**
Non-FR distance questions natively have 3 options; FR has 4. Runtime FR-fallback injected FR's 4th option (in French) onto ~13 of the 20 shown questions, also skewing the max score. Option discovery now prefers **native** options and only falls back to FR when a language has none — which preserves intentionally-untranslated quizzes (e.g. common-points).

### 4. `mariage` result logic
- **Q5 (children):** a mutually-assumed child-free decision was scored as "least ready." Reordered so the genuine misalignment (*one wants kids, the other doesn't*) is lowest and both aligned answers rank high.
- **Q9 (chores):** a harmonious split scored **below** the option that explicitly *"creates tension."* Swapped so tension is the lowest.

### 5. `vrai-faux` (FR) q86 — factual error
"Joséphine de Beauharnais était française" was marked **false**, but she was born in then-French Martinique (her own explanation says so). Corrected to **true**.

## 🟢 UX / retention
Added a prominent **"Share your result"** button to every quiz result screen (Web Share API on mobile, copy-link fallback on desktop with a "link copied" confirmation), localized in all 5 languages using existing i18n keys.

## ✅ Verification
Drove the built site in headless Chromium:
- FR & EN `couple-sain`, healthiest answers → **100% / top tier** (was inverted in non-FR)
- FR `distance` → individual + couple verdicts now render
- Non-FR `distance` → 3 native options, no French leak
- Share button renders per-language on result screens; no JS errors
- Simulated best/worst playthroughs for all scored quizzes in all langs

## 📋 Known issues documented (not changed here — would benefit from a follow-up)
- **`attachement`** (FR-only): attachment *style* is categorical (secure / anxious / avoidant) but is flattened to one linear axis, so it can mislabel anxious-vs-avoidant profiles. Needs a subscore redesign, not a reorder.
- **`divorce`/`toxic`:** the "do you have children" question adds +1 to the toxicity score (it should be context-only), and questions with 5 options weigh slightly more than the 4-option fear/violence questions.
- **non-FR `common-points`:** options are still shown in French (pre-existing translation gap; preserved as-is, not regressed).

author: mcclowes
body:
## Summary

Fixes the three cron-scheduler correctness bugs in #132 (code review H11).

### 1. POSIX day-of-month / day-of-week (OR, not AND)
When **both** day fields are restricted, POSIX cron fires on *either*. The old code `continue`d if *either* failed, ANDing them — so `0 0 13 * 5` ran only on Friday the 13th instead of every 13th **and** every Friday. `getNextCronRun` now tracks whether each day field is a literal `*` and unions them when both are restricted (and applies only the restricted one otherwise).

### 2. Timezone / DST
The schedule used local-time getters with no timezone, so DST broke it twice a year. `getNextCronRun` now evaluates wall-clock fields in a given IANA timezone (default `UTC`, threaded from `schedule.timezone`) via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, and converts the matched wall-clock back to a UTC instant. The DSL already parsed a `timezone` option — the engine now actually honours it. Example: `0 12 * * *` in `America/New_York` resolves to 16:00 UTC in summer (EDT) and 17:00 UTC in winter (EST).

### 3. Drift / missed ticks
`shouldRunNow` fired only if `|now - nextRun| <= 1s`, so a slow run or busy event loop overshot the window and silently skipped the tick (`* * * * *` randomly missed minutes). It's now due when the next scheduled time **after the last run** has passed (`nextRun <= now`) — a late poll still catches the overdue tick. This also fixes never-run cron jobs, which previously computed from the epoch and effectively never matched the window.

(Semantics note: an overdue cron fires **once** when it becomes due, not once per missed minute — no replay storm after an outage. Happy to change to full per-tick replay if that's preferred.)

## Tests
New cases: Friday-the-13th OR semantics; DOM-only and DOW-only wildcards; an EDT/EST DST boundary; `timezone` threading through `getNextRunTime`; and overdue-catch-up vs not-yet-due. Full suite: 1064 passed, 21 skipped (network), `tsc`/lint/format clean.

Fixes #132

author: apelosi
body:
## Why

After #40, `characterMemory` was coming back **`null`** on prod for existing stages. Two causes:
1. **No backfill** — existing characters started at `memory = null` and nothing had generated it.
2. **Serverless cutoff** — the only population path was the *fire-and-forget* refresh after each dialogue line, which runs *after* the response returns and is frequently killed when the function freezes. With agents barely posting (quota issues), almost nothing triggered it.

So `null` was expected — but the population mechanism wasn't reliable. This adds the dependable path.

## What

- **`refreshActiveStageMemories()`** (`lib/stage/character-memory.ts`) — sweeps active stages and runs the existing gated, self-healing per-stage refresh. Has a soft **8s wall-clock budget**: it stops launching new stages once spent, so a large backfill can't blow the cron route's serverless function timeout. Remaining stages are picked up on the next tick (unsummarized characters keep a `null` cursor → retried). Already-summarized stages no-op cheaply, so the budget naturally advances across the full set over a few ticks until everything is backfilled.
- Wired into the existing **`*/30` `turn-open-tick` cron**, running **last** so the cheap housekeeping (safety-net `turn_open`, purge, inactivity flag) always completes even if the budgeted sweep is cut off. **No new scheduled function** (no extra recurring invocation cost).

## Immediate backfill
After this deploys, hit the existing cron endpoint to populate now instead of waiting for the next tick:
```
curl -X POST https://entertheclaw.com/api/cron/turn-open-tick -H "x-cron-secret: <CRON_SECRET>"
```
Run it a few times if there are many stale stages (each call does up to ~8s of memory work, self-healing). Or just wait — the next 30-min tick handles it.

## Verification (dev)
- [x] `tsc` clean
- [x] Sweep scanned 20 active stages, backfilled the test stage's characters, no-op'd the other 19 cheaply
- [x] One slow model call timed out and stayed `null` — self-heals on the next run (cursor only advances on success)

author: bubbleshaker
body:
## 概要

部品（STT / chat / TTS）は中継側で全て実体ありだったが、デバイス側で1本に繋がっておらず「対話」になっていなかった。`sheepOnTap` で得た文字起こし結果 `heard` を中継 `/chat`(Claude Haiku 4.5) に渡し、返答を `speakTts`(ずんだもん) で喋り `drawDialog` に表示する。Close #60

```
タップ → "メェ"でTTS → 録音 → /sttで heard → /chat({message: heard}) → reply → speakTts(reply)＋drawDialog
```

## 変更点

- **`fetchChatReply(message, out)` を新設**：`/chat` に `{message}` を POST し `parse_relay_reply` で `ReplyMessage` に。Claude 推論は数秒かかるため `/stt` と同様 `setTimeout(20000)`（既定5秒だと -11）。
- **`fetchGreeting` を `fetchChatReply` へ委譲**（DRY／重複した HTTP 構築を解消）。
- **`sheepOnTap` の末尾を拡張**：`heard` 非空なら chat → `drawDialog` 表示 → `speakTts`。発話時間を `speaking_duration_ms` で見積もり「喋る間だけ揺れる」を維持。揺れ起点は録音+chat で数秒経つため `now` でなく最新 `millis()`（#58 と同じ桁あふれ回避）。
- オフライン/上流失敗時は従来どおり何もしないフォールバック。

## テスト・検証

- `pio run -e m5stack-cores3`: SUCCESS
- `pio test -e native`: 93 cases すべて PASS（回帰なし）
- 純粋ロジック（`parse_relay_reply` は test_net、`speaking_duration_ms` は test_avatar で網羅済み）。本変更は HTTP 副作用層のみのため新規 native テストは無し。

## Summary

- The default (no-image) avatar lost all background color: it rendered as initials on a transparent circle.
- Root cause: `getAvatarBackground` picked from a 6-entry palette where half the entries referenced CSS variables `--forest-600/700/800`. Those variables are only defined in `pkgs/design-tokens/mosoo.css`, which the web app does not import, so `background: var(--forest-600)` resolved to nothing. Any account whose seed hashed to a forest entry showed no fill (e.g. `22@mosoo.ai`, reported in the issue).

- Restores the intended "solid color avatar" behavior. Literal hex values remove the hidden dependency on un-imported theme tokens, so the fill can never silently disappear again.

author: purplechoims
body:
### Motivation
- The Playwright/Chromium fallback followed attacker-controlled navigations without the curl transport's SSRF/per-hop RoE checks, allowing final browser URLs (loopback, RFC1918, metadata, etc.) to reach the agent.
- Because the sandbox image now installs Chromium and the Playwright template deps by default, the browser tier became a reachable escalation path that must enforce the same safety checks as the curl grid.
- The change aims to ensure the browser fallback either inherits the same SSRF safety and RoE gating or is suppressed when curl already blocked an unsafe redirect.

### Description
- Threaded a `scope_check` parameter into `run_playwright_fallback` and the fetch chain so per-hop RoE gating can be enforced for fallback runs.
- After the Node template returns, `executor.run_playwright_fallback` now classifies the `finalUrl` via `safety.classify_url` and rejects/block-returns when the final URL is private/blocked or out of RoE scope instead of trusting the browser output.
- `fetch_chain` prevents invoking the browser fallback if the curl transport trace already recorded an `ssrf_redirect_blocked:` error to avoid retrying an attacker-controlled URL with the browser tier.
- Playwright templates (desktop + mobile) now install a request-interception safety guard that resolves and classifies every request (including NAT64/unwrapped IPv4-mapped IPv6 handling via `ipaddr.js`) and aborts requests that resolve to private/loopback/link-local/reserved or fail DNS resolution; `ipaddr.js` was added to the templates' `package.json`.
- Added unit tests covering the new behaviors: blocking a private final URL and blocking an out-of-scope final URL, while preserving successful fallback behavior.

### Testing
- Ran the sandbox_web unit tests with the node subprocess mocked: `DECEPTICON_SKIP_BOOT=1 pytest packages/decepticon/tests/unit/sandbox_web/test_executor.py packages/decepticon/tests/unit/sandbox_web/test_fetch_chain.py packages/decepticon/tests/unit/sandbox_web/test_safety.py` and observed all tests pass (`20 passed, 1 warning`).
- Performed Node syntax checks: `node --check` on both Playwright templates and `python -m py_compile` on modified Python modules, both succeeded with no syntax errors.
- Verified that template dependency changes were limited to adding `ipaddr.js` and that `git diff --check` produced no whitespace or trailing-eol issues.

author: richardwooding
body:
The `review` gate scored only **cyclomatic** complexity. Now that cognitive complexity is computed for Go + most tree-sitter languages, the gate gains a cognitive threshold — a distinct, often better signal, because it weights *nesting* and so catches deeply-nested code a modest cyclomatic count misses.

## What
- `ReviewConfig.MaxCognitive` (default 15): a changed-file function whose cognitive complexity exceeds it is a **fail**-level finding, rule `cognitive-complexity`. Only applies where cognitive is available (`fn.CognitiveComplexity != nil`) — a function in an unsupported language (Swift) is never flagged on this gate.
- A function may trip both gates (separate findings/rules) — cyclomatic and cognitive are independent signals.
- CLI `--max-cognitive`, MCP `max_cognitive`, both default 15. SARIF surfaces it as `review-cognitive-complexity`.

## Why it matters
A function with 6 nested `if`s has cyclomatic **7** (under the default gate) but cognitive **21** (over it). The new test proves the cognitive gate flags it while the cyclomatic gate stays silent — exactly the hard-to-read code the old gate let through.

## Testing
- New `TestReview_FlagsCognitiveComplexity` (cyclomatic 7 / cognitive 21 → only the cognitive rule fires).
- Existing review tests still pass (the branchy-function test now also gets a cognitive finding, verdict unchanged).
- `go build`/`vet`/`go fix` clean; search/mcpserver/cmd suites green.

Lands after v0.112.0 (just released), so it ships in the next release.

author: sag333ar
body:
Parses two new BIP21 URI parameters and routes them through the existing payment flow:

  - `op_return=<hex>`: hex-encoded payload (up to 80 bytes) attached to the transaction as a 0-value OP_RETURN output. Used for cross-chain memos (THORChain/Maya), order IDs, and similar payee-side correlation data.

  - `callback=<https-url>`: https URL opened in a Chrome Custom Tab after a successful send so the merchant can continue its checkout flow. Only https is accepted at parse time to prevent a URI from invoking arbitrary app handlers.

The OP_RETURN payload is built via `ScriptBuilder.createOpReturnScript` and appended to the existing `outputs[]` array, so the existing broadcast path picks it up with no further changes. The dust check in bitcoinj's `TransactionOutput.isDust` already exempts 0-value OP_RETURN scripts, so no special-case handling was needed there.

`mergeWithEditedValues` now preserves auxiliary outputs (e.g. OP_RETURN) and the callback URL when the user edits the amount in the send screen — previously the non-primary outputs were dropped.

Both parameters are optional and additive — URIs that don't carry them behave identically to before.

Mirrors the corresponding iOS change in dashpay/dashsync-iOS and dashpay/dashwallet-ios.

author: nicoloboschi
body:
Fixes #2386.

## Problem

The Claude Code plugin is distributed via the **marketplace manifest**, not a package registry. The integration release flow (`scripts/release-integration.sh claude-code <version>`) already bumps `hindsight-integrations/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, but the marketplace manifest carried **no `version`** and was never bumped — so the published catalog never reflected new releases, and shipped fixes (e.g. the Windows venv fix in #2066) didn't surface as updates.

## Fix

Keep releasing the Claude Code plugin exactly as before, but also bump the marketplace version as part of that release:

- Add a `"version"` field to the root `/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — the public `vectorize-io/hindsight` marketplace (`claude plugin marketplace add vectorize-io/hindsight`).
- `scripts/release-integration.sh` now bumps that version in lockstep with the plugin version whenever `claude-code` is released, and stages it in the release commit. For every other integration this is a no-op.

## Cleanup: removed the redundant second manifest

There were **two** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` files. Per the official Claude Code docs, `claude plugin marketplace add owner/repo` only ever reads the **root** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (no recursive subdir scan), and `--sparse <paths>` only limits the checkout footprint — it still reads the root manifest. So `hindsight-integrations/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (added in #661 on the assumption that `--sparse hindsight-integrations` would read it) was never actually consulted by any install path. Its only mention was a stale CI echo string.

- **Delete** `hindsight-integrations/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
- **Fix** the stale `--sparse hindsight-integrations` install hint in `release-integration.yml` to the documented plain form.

The claude-code release flow is otherwise unchanged — release it as before.

## Note

Per the Claude Code plugin docs, a plugin's version resolves from `plugin.json` first, then the marketplace entry, then the git SHA — so `plugin.json` (already bumped by the release) is the primary update signal; this PR keeps the marketplace manifest version in sync so the catalog advertises the release too. The underlying reason 0.7.2–0.8.3 didn't reach users was simply that the claude-code release wasn't cut for those versions; cutting it now (with this change) bumps `plugin.json` + the marketplace manifest together.

author: lepy
body:
## Überblick

`sdata` nutzt jetzt das eigenständige **`suuid` (>=0.2.0)** als Single Source of Truth für semantische, **100% S3-sichere** IDs (`Class__safe_name__huuid`). `sdata/suuid.py` ist nur noch ein dünner Adapter.

## Änderungen

- **`sdata/suuid.py`** — Adapter (Subclass von `suuid.SUUID`) mit Rückwärtskompatibilitäts-Aliassen:
  `suuid_str`/`suuid_bytes` → `compact_token`, `uuid`/`get_uuid` → `as_uuid`,
  `from_name(ns_name=…)` → `ns=…`, `from_suuid_sname` → `from_sname(strict=False)`,
  `from_suuid_str`/`from_suuid_bytes` → `from_compact_token`,
  `generate_safe_filename` → `suuid.safe_name`, plus `from_uuid`/`from_obj`/`to_list`/`to_dict`/`is_valid_suuid_str`.
  Erbt Immutabilität, Wertgleichheit und die eingefrorene Normalisierung.
- **`sdata/base.py`** — SUUID-Erzeugung vereinheitlicht auf deterministisches `from_name` (ns-gescopt); kein Direkt-Konstruktor mehr.
- **`setup.py`** — `suuid>=0.2.0` als Core-Dependency.
- **Tests** — `test_suuid`/`test_suuid_class` auf den Adapter neu geschrieben (huuid-Goldenwerte bleiben gültig, da gleicher uuid5-Algorithmus); 2 `test_base`-Werte auf das `__`-Format aktualisiert.

## Tests (lokal, `./ci/local-ci.sh`)

- `test_suuid` + `test_suuid_class` + `test_base`: **47/47 grün**.

author: alexdima
body:
## What

Removes the external DTD declaration from the minimal fontconfig config that the Linux smoke-test job installs as a workaround for the expat 2.6.1 NULL-deref CVEs.

```diff
  <?xml version="1.0"?>
- <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
  <fontconfig>
```

## Why

The job already sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE=/tmp/fonts-minimal.conf` with `<include>` removed to avoid the expat external-entity crash path. But a flaky smoke-test failure ([run 28140700565](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/28140700565/job/83337233535), `Linux / Electron-Smoke`) still crashed with that workaround active.

I pulled the crash-dump artifact and walked the minidump. The faulting thread was a **SIGSEGV (NULL deref, fault address 0x0)** with this native stack:

```
libc.so.6
libfontconfig.so.1   (config parsing)
libexpat.so.1        (XML / external-entity parsing)
...Chromium browser-process font-init frames...
```

i.e. the crash is in **libexpat called from libfontconfig during Chromium's browser-process font initialization at startup** — not in VS Code/Chromium logic. The dump confirms `FONTCONFIG_FILE=/tmp/fonts-minimal.conf` was in effect and the minimal config was loaded.

The remaining trigger is the `<!DOCTYPE … SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">` line: fontconfig feeds that DTD to expat as an external **parameter** entity, which still hits the not-yet-backported `CVE-2026-32776` / `CVE-2026-32778` NULL-deref paths on expat 2.6.1 even after `<include>` was removed. fontconfig does not require the DOCTYPE, so dropping it removes the last external-entity codepath.

## Validation

- Workflow YAML parses (PyYAML `safe_load`).
- The generated config (DOCTYPE removed) parses as valid XML; the diagnostics step's `ElementTree.parse` does not fetch external DTDs, so it is unaffected.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is a mitigation. The durable fix is shipping `libexpat >= 2.7.5` on the runner; the step already auto-disables the whole workaround when it detects that version.
- Companion harness PR #322905 makes such a launch crash fail fast with an actionable error instead of a 120s opaque Mocha `before all` hook timeout.

author: jonjon-prog
body:
Hey Afadil! 👋

This fixes a regression where the rebalance planner in scope "All" with whole-share mode  and fractional mode produces "no valid price for modes". 
Skipped." for **every** asset,  no trades at all.

## Root cause

Commit `0b87d036` (fix: load per-account holdings when cash overrides exist) introduced `get_holdings_for_allocation()` in `AllocationService`. 
When cash allocation overrides exist (account with `cashCategoryId` in meta), this function returns **non-aggregated** holdings with per-account IDs (`"{prefix}-{account_id}-{asset_id}"`).

Meanwhile, `rebalance_service.rs` builds its price map from `get_holdings_for_accounts()` which always **aggregates** holdings (IDs = `"AGG-{instrument_id}"`).

The contributions (from `AllocationService`) use the non-aggregated holding IDs, but the price map uses aggregated IDs → **no key ever matches** → "Missing quote" for every asset.

Individual account scope works because with a single account there's no aggregation.
Bboth paths produce the same IDs.

## Fix

Key the price/quantity maps by **instrument ID** (via a new `asset_key()` helper) instead of `holding.id`, and group contributions by `asset_id` instead of `holding_id` in `build_candidates` / `build_sell_candidates`.

The instrument ID is the stable identifier across both aggregated and per-account holding paths — it's also what `AllocationService::holding_display()` uses to derive `contribution.asset_id`.

## Testing

- `cargo check --workspace` ✅
- `cargo test -p wealthfolio-core` — all tests pass ✅  
- Manual: scope "All" whole-share mode now produces buy/sell trades correctly

---

Round 4 from `docs/claude_review.md` (A1, B9, E3, E10), built on a shared run-index foundation. The old `/history` walked the entire output tree and opened every run's JSON on each request; this replaces that with a small SQLite index.

## A1 — Run index (the foundation)
New `application/index.py` (`RunIndex`): a SQLite cache at `OUTPUT_ROOT/index.db`, treated as a **derived view** — the per-run JSON files remain the source of truth.
- `AnalysisService` adds each new GUI run to the index live.
- `reconcile()` runs on startup to sync with disk: adds runs created outside the service (e.g. the CLI) and drops rows for purged folders.
- Thread-safe (`check_same_thread=False` + a lock) because `analyze()` now runs on background-job threads.

## B9 — Pagination
`/history?page=N` (24 per page) via indexed `LIMIT/OFFSET`, with Prev/Next controls and a "X runs · page N of M" summary.

## E3 — Search + filter
`?q=` case-insensitive name search and `?tier=` imagery-tier filter chips, both preserved across pagination.

## E10 — Runs map
A Leaflet map on the History page with a pin per located run (auto-fit bounds, click-to-open), fed by `RunIndex.points()`.

## Tests
47 pass (+6 for the index: add/upsert, pagination, search, tier filter, points-skip-unlocated, reconcile add+drop). New `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture isolates `OUTPUT_ROOT` so the suite never reads/writes the real `output_images/`. The full `/history` flow (reconcile → paginate → search → tier → map) was also verified end-to-end via TestClient with 27 seeded runs.

author: rexbron
body:
Fixes #150 — expanding a collapsed list of call/system events would clip the content and push the timeline off screen.

### Cause
The table-backed timeline renderer caches row heights keyed by `(messageID, width)`. Expanding a collapsed group only flips the shared `@Observable ExpandedGroupsState` — it doesn't change the `rows` data, so `updateRows` never diffs that row, the height cache keeps the **collapsed** value, and `heightOfRow` returns it. NSTableView then clips the taller expanded content to the old height, and the un-accounted-for growth throws off scroll position.

### Fix
- `ExpandedGroupsState.toggle` now fires an `onToggle(groupID)` callback after mutating.
- The table controller's new `remeasureRow(forMessageID:)` invalidates that row's cached height and calls `noteHeightOfRows`. `heightOfRow`'s measurement host rebuilds the row reading the updated expansion state, so it returns the full expanded (or collapsed) height.
- Scroll position is preserved across the height change, so expanding a row above the viewport no longer shifts the visible content off screen.
- The representable wires `expandedGroups.onToggle` to the controller.

The LazyVStack renderer auto-sizes and was never affected — this is specific to the table renderer's height cache.

### Testing
- Expand/collapse a collapsed group of call/membership events → the row grows/shrinks to fit instead of clipping, and the timeline stays put.

author: afadesigns
body:
## What

Stop ZC1044 ("use `cd … || return`") from flagging an assignment to a variable named `cd`.

`(( flag )) && cd=${cd/#$HOME/~}` assigns to a variable `cd`. On the right of `&&`/`||` the parser reads `cd=value` as a `cd` command whose first argument is the `=value` tail, so the kata flagged it as an unguarded directory change. The cd builtin never takes an argument beginning with `=`, so this shape is now recognised as the assignment and skipped.

## Why

The advice is meaningless on an assignment — there is no directory change to guard. The root cause is a parser quirk: an assignment word is recognised at statement start but parsed as a command after `&&`/`||`. The full parser fix is broader and risk-bearing (it shifts how every `cmd && var=value` parses), so this guards the kata precisely while the parser fix is tracked separately.

## Verification

- AST confirmed: `foo && cd=$bar` parses to `SimpleCommand{Name: cd, Args: ["=$bar"]}`; a real `cd /tmp` has no `=`-prefixed argument.
- Removes 1 finding from the violation baseline (zsh-z); a real unguarded `cd`, including `foo && cd /tmp`, still fires.
- Regression test in `pkg/katas/katatests/fp_round6_test.go`; `go test ./...` passes, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, sweeps clean.

La nueva función `/.netlify/functions/verify-pro-access` normalizó el correo, revisó la base de datos local de usuarios y suscripciones, aceptó únicamente estados `active` o `trialing`, y respondió con el estado, plan y fecha de renovación. Cuando no encontró una suscripción local, consultó Stripe por el correo, buscó una suscripción activa o en prueba, y sincronizó el registro en Netlify Database para que el acceso quedara disponible en visitas posteriores.

La interfaz ahora guardó una sesión local de respaldo visual después de una verificación exitosa, mostró “Vitalis Pro activo”, ocultó los botones de pago, desbloqueó el protocolo completo, activó el mensaje de consultas ilimitadas y mostró contenido exclusivo. Para correos no reconocidos, mostró el mensaje solicitado, permitió intentar otro correo y ofreció contacto de soporte.

También se mantuvieron visibles las credenciales del Dr. José Rogelio Sánchez García en el sitio y dentro de la consulta, incluyendo especialidad, diplomado, cédulas profesionales y el Centro de Salud Sexual Masculina.
